### F0, the net and the record: done, and what a later piece should know

Two tools of the harness, and no line of the program: `VC.EXE` is the
same bytes before and after.

**The two commands of the image**, for a piece that is to change
nothing that the program does:

    python3 harness/dataimage.py save build/portable_c/VC.EXE build/before
    python3 harness/dataimage.py compare build/before build/portable_c/images

The first, with the build that the piece starts from, before anything
is changed: it takes the program through every scenario and keeps what
it has in its memory at the end of each, holding it to no golden; two
to three and a half minutes by the load. The second, when the
piece's own build has been through `portable_c-scenarios`, which writes
the same images of the build that it judges into `images` next to the
program. In place of the first, `cp -r build/portable_c/images
build/before` does, if the test has just run on the build that the
piece starts from; and where "before" has to be made again later, of
the commit that the piece now stands on, `save` takes any `VC.EXE` with
its `VC.MAP` next to it, in a directory called `portable_c`, as a copy
of the tree that is built beside has it. The images are of a build, 3.7
MB for all scenarios, and are under `build/`, never committed. The top
of `harness/dataimage.py` says what an image is and how it is read.

**When it is taken.** The driver of the tests resets the machine when
it has written the last step's screen, which it does when the program
waits for a key with nothing left to do. QEMU is told, by its
`set-action`, to pause a machine that would end, and the memory is read
there with `pmemsave` (`linger` and `memory` of `harness/dos.py`): the
same instruction in every run. Nothing of the driver or of the bench
changed for it, and every golden derived again leaves
`harness/goldens/` as it was. That the machine has come to its end QEMU
says by itself, and the harness listens: asking QEMU a hundred times a
second, which was the first try, took 25 seconds of a run of 100.

**What is steady**, tried with all 155 scenarios:

| Held against each other | What differs |
|---|---|
| The same build, three times: twice by the scenarios' test, with QEMU's log of what ran, on a machine that did little else and on one that did more, and once by `save`, without the log, with ten other machines running | Nothing, in any scenario: not a byte of the program's data, the stack included (9 scenarios were held whole, the rest as the tool holds them) |
| The same build with the driver writing the program's stack out at every step, as the test has it, and without | 20 scenarios, in `Rand1` and `Rand2`, `Stars`, `MousTim`, the time of a file in the `DTA` and in a panel's list. The program is the same, but it gets to a step some instructions later, and these follow the time. `save` takes the scenarios as the test does for that reason, and `save --early` as it does not: the way to see whether a thing follows the time, with one build |
| A build whose data the linker has laid out otherwise, two variables added and nothing else: the main data 40 bytes on, the 640 KB 64 | `OwnFirst` of `dos32.c` in every scenario, a paragraph on; the seven words of the main data that hold a segment; two more segments that the program had left in its buffers, `TmpBuf+128` after a copy and `MenuBuf+48` after a dialog; and one pointer of a variable, in every scenario. No time, since no instruction is another |
| A build that takes 20 instructions more for every round of its wait for a key | 9 scenarios, in the same fields as the second row but `MousTim` |

So the image is steady from run to run and under load, which answers
10 of "What could go wrong": no read of memory that was never written
shows, in any scenario. And two builds differ, with no fault in either,
in what follows the time and in what holds an address, and in nothing
else that was seen.

**What is left out, and how.** All of it is in `harness/dataimage.py`,
each with its reason:

- `ADDRESSES`: the seven words of the main data that hold a segment or
  a count of paragraphs, `WCB1seg`, `WCB2seg`, `WCBcrn`, `WCBsec`,
  `ViewSeg`, `MemSeg`, `FreMem2`. Not left out but held by what they
  name: the block and how far into it. A word that names another place
  in one build than in the other is a difference.
- A word of the main data that differs and is a segment of the same
  place of the same block in both builds, and a variable of four bytes
  or a multiple whose words differ and name the same thing by the two
  maps: counted in the last line of the summary, and no difference.
  That is cheap, and it is all that is known of a pointer: where there
  is one is not known, only that two numbers that differ name one
  thing. A pointer in the main data or in a block is not looked for;
  the plan has none there.
- `UNSTEADY`, 140 bytes of the main data: `Rand1`, `Rand2`, `Stars`,
  `MousTim`, and the time and date in the `DTA`. `UNSTEADY_VARIABLES`:
  `OwnFirst`. `UNSTEADY_ENTRY`: `TimeF` of an entry of a panel's list,
  and the same bytes where a copy of the list lies behind the panels.
  These are compared, printed with `--all`, counted as "may differ",
  and fail nothing.
- The stack, 16 KB: return addresses, another thing in every build.
- A block that is free, and the paragraph that `dos32.c` keeps in front
  of each block: the lengths of the blocks and which are taken are held
  in their place.
- What is not the program's data at all: the registers, the screen, the
  extender's memory and DOS's, where `dos32.c` has its block of real
  mode.

What is then held, in a scenario: the main data, 62,603 bytes but for
those 140 and the 14 of the addresses; the blocks that are taken, all
655,360 bytes in most scenarios, the panels and whatever is behind
them, written or not; the 937 bytes of the variables that the map names
outside the main data, by the file and the name of each; and the 25,080
bytes of the tables, which are held against the program's own file as
the extender loads it, when the image is taken, so a write into a table
shows with no second build.

`python3 harness/dataimage.py check DIRECTORY` holds a directory of
images against itself and then against copies with one byte changed, in
the main data, in a panel's structure, in an entry of its list, behind
the panels, at the end of the block, in a variable and in a word that
holds a segment: each has to be named, and is, as "the main data,
TmpBuf+3" or "the panel of WCB1seg, entry 2 of its list, AttrF".

**How a piece says what it means to change.**

- `--changed NAME`, once for each: a field of the main data, a
  structure that lies over one, `EdData`, `ViewDat`, `FndData` or
  `HlpData`, a variable as `file.Name`, a thing in a block as `"the
  panel of WCB1seg"` or `"behind the panels"`, or `"the blocks"` for
  how many blocks there are and how long each is. What differs
  there is printed with `[declared]` and fails nothing. The commit says
  the same. A piece that widens a field of a structure laid over a
  buffer names the structure so: the fields behind the one that grew
  are then at other places, and the tool, which names a byte by the
  original's listing, says the old names for them.
- A word that leaves the main data for a pointer beside it, as F1's
  three and F2's four: its line of `ADDRESSES` gets `variable=("main",
  "_Name")`, the file and the symbol as the linker's map has them. A
  build that has the variable is read there, as a pointer, and one that
  has not is read in the field, so the build before and the build after
  are held against each other by what the word names. The field's two
  bytes are not compared in either. That edit is committed with the
  piece.
- A thing that differs and follows the time: `save --early` of the
  piece's own build into a third directory, and `compare` of that with
  the piece's images. If it differs there too, it follows the time and
  gets a line of `UNSTEADY` with its reason, which is a change to the
  net and is said in the commit; if it does not, the piece has changed
  what the program writes.

**Where the blocks are, now and when the extender has them.** The tool
knows no address but that of the program's data on the bench, which the
driver of the tests goes by too (`le.BENCH`): the main data is at `_md`
of the map, and the blocks are read from what `dos32.c` keeps in front
of each inside `Own`, which the map names. What is compared of the
blocks is what the program has in them, by name: "the panel of
WCB1seg", "the panel of WCB2seg" and "behind the panels", each from
where its word of `ADDRESSES` says to the next of them or to the end
of its block. So they are the same things whether the program cuts
them out of one block, as today, or has a block for each, as from F1
on, wherever the blocks lie; and an address is held by which of them
it is in and how far. Where two builds have one of them of two
lengths, as F1's will have each panel and the room, it is held as far
as both have it and the two lengths are said, which `--changed "the
blocks"` declares, with how many blocks there are and how long. What
lies behind the end of a panel's list in the build that has the panel
longer is then held against what the other build happens to have
there: F1 reads those, if there are any.

With the memory from the extender, F9, a block lies wherever the
extender put it, outside the program's data. The image has room for that: it is
a list of stretches, each with a name, an address and a length, and
`_handed` of `harness/dataimage.py` is where the list is made, empty
today. What it needs is a line of `dos32.c`, which was not F0's to
make: **a table of the blocks that the program holds, each with its
address and its length, as a variable that the linker's map names**,
and the count of them. `dos32.c` will have such a table in any case,
for the handle that the extender wants back with each block. The tool
then takes each stretch with the same `pmemsave`, at the address of the
table, which is right for as long as the extender's memory is where
the machine's is, as it is on the bench. Whoever moves the memory
writes `_handed` and `_blocks` for the table, and `check` says whether
the net still catches a byte in a block.

**The 16 bytes round a block, for F1.** The extender keeps 16 bytes
of its own between two blocks and ends a program that has written into
them; the 640 KB take such a write without a sign. So from F1 on the
hand-out of the 640 KB keeps 16 bytes of a pattern round its blocks,
and the tool holds them: `guards` of `harness/dataimage.py`, at the
moment an image is taken. A scenario whose image has them otherwise
fails `portable_c-scenarios` whatever its screens show, with a line
that names the scenario, the block and the first byte that is another,
and `save` and `compare` say the same of their images. It is built and
tried, with what the image has in front of its first block today taken
for a pattern, right and then wrong by a byte, through a scenario and
in `check`; and it looks at nothing until a pattern is declared. What
F1 tells the tool, in that file:

- `GUARD`: the pattern, as the 16 bytes that `dos32.c` writes.
- `_guarded`: where they are. As it stands: the bytes that end where
  each block that is taken begins, and those that begin where the last
  block of the memory ends, taken or not. Today the paragraph in front
  of a block is where `dos32.c` keeps the block's length, and the last
  block ends where `Own` does, to within the 15 bytes that round it to
  a paragraph: F1 gives the pattern its room in both places, and makes
  `_guarded` say what it has made.
- `_blocks`: the blocks, which it reads from that paragraph in front of
  each. If the hand-out keeps its blocks otherwise, a table, this reads
  the table, by the symbol of the map that names it.

A pattern that is not in the image, behind the end of the program's
data, is said as that and fails too.

**What the next pieces should know.**

- The scenarios' test writes the images of every run, into
  `build/portable_c/images`: the next run of the test overwrites them.
  Keep "before" elsewhere, before the first build of the piece.
- The test holds nothing by the images. A piece is held to them by its
  own `compare`, and says in its commit what that printed in its last
  lines.
- A scenario that did not get to its end has no image, and `compare`
  fails for one that only one side has.
- An image is of the first copy of the program. Where a scenario ends
  in a second copy, started from the command line, that one's memory
  is not in it.
- Two builds whose code differs are expected to print "as before, but
  for what may differ" for some ten to twenty scenarios, and "0
  differences".
- The time that the saving costs: 0.4 seconds of reading the machines'
  memory, 1.2 of packing and writing and 0.2 of asking QEMU, for all
  155 scenarios together and summed over the four that run side by
  side. Against the test's own time that is not to be measured on a
  machine that others use: by the clock the test took 217 and 311
  seconds with images and 222 and 322 without, by the load, and the
  whole suite 271 and 478 seconds with them. By the processors' time,
  which the load moves less, 48 scenarios as the test runs them took
  190 and 204 seconds without images and 197 and 210 with, in the
  order 190, 197, 204, 210 as the load rose from 3 to 7.

**The record of the words.** `harness/words.py` counts how often each
word of the addresses is written in each file of `src/portable_c`,
`harness/words.txt` has the counts, and the test `portable_c-words`
holds the tree to them, fewer as well as more, as `portable_c-host`
holds it to its own: `python3 harness/words.py --record` in the commit
that moves a count, and the record's lines there say what went. A run
prints the table of the words: the places and the files of each, the
file with the most, and the piece that is to have it at nothing. As F0
leaves it, by that piece: F1 68 places, F2 536, F3 277, F5 45, F6 44,
F7 67, F8 212, F10 198; `ENTRY`, `DSKBUF`, `TRELIST`, `NUMBER_OF` and
the three of the tables stay. What it counts besides the words of
`vc.h`: `md.NAME` for the twelve words of the main data that hold a
segment or a place, `u16 panel` and `u16 segment` for a segment kept in
a number, and `AddressOf` and `OFFSET_OF` of the editor. Three things
to know:

- A word is counted in the body of another's definition, so `vc.h` has
  `AT` and `ARENA` for as long as `PANEL` and `OFFSET` are made of
  them.
- A word of the addresses that a piece adds to `vc.h` is named in
  `WORDS` of `harness/words.py`, with the piece that is to have it at
  nothing, as it is named in `WORDS` of `harness/int16.py`.
- A segment that is kept under another name than `panel` or `segment`,
  `other`, `top`, `behind`, is not counted: 4 of "What could go wrong"
  stands.
- The table says which piece is to have a word at nothing; the test
  does not hold a piece to it. `SEG_OF`, `OFFSET_IN_SEG` and `AT` go up
  first, at every place where a piece meets what another still has as
  a segment.

### F1, three blocks where there was one: done, and what a later piece should know

The program has a block for each panel and one for the room, inside
the 640 KB, and nothing is moved any more. All 155 scenarios pass with
no golden and no patch changed, at the first run.

**What it is now.**

- `Init11` takes two blocks of `PANEL_BLOCK`, 1000h paragraphs, and
  then the largest that there is, the room. `GiveMem` gives the room
  back and `TakeMem` takes the largest block again; neither touches a
  panel. `Aexec0` makes the room as short as `ROOM_LEAST` and then as
  long as it goes. `ReDr00` and `ReDr50` of `read.c` have lost their
  halves that moved the other panel up and down, 60 lines: the list's
  limit is what the original has with memory enough, a paragraph short
  of 64K less two entries, and the old list is kept where the room
  begins.
- Beside the main data, in `main.c`: `Room`, where the room begins, and
  `RoomEnd`, where it ends, both `u8 *`. `RoomParas()` of `start.c` is
  the one function that says how long the room is, in paragraphs of 16
  bits. `ViewSeg`, `MemSeg` and `FreMem2` are in `struct MainDat` with
  "Not set or read here". Two pointers and not three: `MemSeg` was the
  block that all of it was in and has no successor, and `ViewSeg` no
  longer moves, so where the room begins is its block.
- Elsewhere `SEG_OF(Room)`, 22 places in `copy.c`, `edit.c`, `find.c`,
  `view.c`, `files.c` and `start.c`, by one line of a script.
- `dos32.c` keeps what it knows of its blocks in a table beside the
  memory, `OwnBlocks` with `OwnHeld`, where it kept a paragraph in front
  of each block in the memory itself. That paragraph holds the pattern
  now, F0h down to E1h, written when the block is taken, and the last
  paragraph of the memory holds it from the start. So the room is
  0x7FFD paragraphs, 524,240 bytes, on any machine: 640 KB and a
  paragraph, less two panels and four paragraphs of the pattern.

**What the plan had wrong or had not.**

- "The room equal where it was written" does not hold against the
  build before, and cannot. The original keeps the old list of a
  directory that is read behind the panel as it is moved up, some 64K
  beyond where the room begins afterwards; with nothing moved it is
  where the room begins. So the room's bytes differ from the build
  before in 142 of 155 scenarios, by where things lie in it and by what
  each has left under the next. See "The image" for what held it
  instead.
- `ReDr50` moves a panel too, down again, and was not named.
- The 16 bytes cost the hand-out its place for what it keeps of a
  block. The plan's 64 bytes are right only with that in a table, which
  F0's section had as F9's. It is F1's now, and `_blocks` of the
  image's tool reads it.
- `PANEL_PARAS` and `VIEW_PARAS` are gone as the record wants, and a
  count of paragraphs is still what the functions for the memory take:
  `PANEL_BLOCK`, `ROOM_LEAST` and `RoomParas` are in `WORDS` of
  `harness/words.py` for F9, which makes them bytes.
- What `Init11` answers where there is too little: the paragraphs that
  there were for the room, or for a panel that got none. On the bench
  neither can happen, the memory being the program's own.
- `copy-big` gets to its point again, and `editor-full` does not:
  below.
- The image's tool looked for the pattern in the images of the build
  before as soon as it was declared, and said of each that it was not
  there. A build is known to write the pattern by having the table.
- The clock's separator follows the hundredths of a second, and is in
  the program's copy of the screen: `clock-path` differed in that byte
  against the build before, which takes thousands of instructions more
  to a step for the panels that it moves, where `save --early` of the
  piece's own build did not differ. It is in `UNSTEADY` by reading
  `Input` of `input.c`, not by F0's trial, which is too fine for it.

**The image, and how it was read.** Three sets of images: of the build
before, saved before anything was changed; of the piece's build, as the
scenarios' test left them; and of a third build made for this alone, in
`build/` and not kept: the source before with its panels fixed at 64K,
three lines, `PANEL_PARAS` 0x1000, `OWN_PARAGRAPHS` 0x9FFD so that its
room is as long as the piece's, and in `ReDr50` the place that the
other panel is moved down to made `panel + 0x1000`. That build does
what the original's routines do and moves nothing, since everything is
where it would be moved to.

| Held against the piece's build | Declared | What was left |
|---|---|---|
| The third build | `FreMem2`, `MemSeg`, `the blocks`, `ViewSeg`, `dos32.OwnCount` | Two runs of bytes in one scenario, `view-commands`: three bytes at +8000 of the room, where the old hand-out wrote what it kept of the free block behind the room while a viewer of another's ran. Everything else equal in all 155: the main data, both panels in all of their 64K, all 524,240 bytes of the room, the variables. "2 differences, 467 more in what was declared as changed, 191 in what may differ" |
| The build before | `FreMem2`, `MemSeg`, `the blocks`, `ViewSeg` | 17,722 differences in 144 scenarios, of two kinds. The room, in 142 scenarios, for the reason above. And in the main data what follows the room's length: the editor's count of free bytes as digits, in `TmpErr` and at the start of `TmpBuf`, in 27 scenarios; `EdSpace` and `ViSpace`; `FndSize`, 8,064 lines for 9,873, in five; and in `copy-big` how much was read, the source's handle and a cell of the bar. No panel differs as far as the build before has it, and no variable. With those declared too, `behind the panels`, `TmpErr`, `TmpBuf`, `ErrBuf`: "0 differences, 18652 more in what was declared as changed, 209 in what may differ" |

What each declared name is: `FreMem2` names the end of the room, which
is another length; `MemSeg` is 0 where it was a segment; `the blocks`
are three where there was one; `ViewSeg`, in `start-memory` alone,
names a room that is given back when the image is taken, which the
build before has as the end of its block made short; `dos32.OwnCount`
is the third build's own.

So the judgement rests on the third build. Declaring the room and
`TmpBuf` as changed against the build before would have passed
anything.

**The pattern, tried.** A line at the end of `Init11` that writes a 0
behind the end of the first panel's block, not committed:
`portable_c-scenarios` failed for all 155, each with "the 16 bytes in
front of block 1 are not the pattern, from the byte at +0 of them on",
and `save` says the same. `python3 harness/dataimage.py check` catches
a byte in each kind of place in the piece's images and in those of the
build before.

**The scenarios that the plan names**, with the room at 524,240 bytes:

| Scenario | What it does |
|---|---|
| `start-memory`, `second-copy`, `command`, `enter-many` | Pass. `enter-many` holds the 256 files, which are cut as they were: question 4 is not touched |
| `copy-big` | Reads its file of 526,632 bytes in two parts again, the first of 523,776, and is skipped with not all of it read: `CpRead` and the source's handle in the image say so. It gets to its point, as it did not while the room was 641,824 bytes |
| `editor-full` | Passes, and is still never full: 130,270 bytes free at its end, where the build before had 247,854 and the original has none |

| `view-window` | Passes: a megabyte is refused as it was |

Entry 13 of `DEVIATIONS.md` has the new figures and entry 1 the three
blocks.

**The records.** The words that were F1's are at nothing: `md.ViewSeg`
38, `md.MemSeg` 14, `md.FreMem2` 8, `PANEL_PARAS` 6, `VIEW_PARAS` 2.
Left to go, by piece: F2 496, where it was 536, since `read.c` and
`start.c` lost 40 mentions of a panel with what moved them; F3 277;
F5 45; F6 44; F7 67; F8 212; F9 13, new; F10 211, where it was 198,
`SEG_OF` being up by 22 and `MAIN_SEG` down by 8. `harness/int16.txt` has one place more,
`RoomParas`, with its reason. The host check's record did not move.

**How long it took**, in tool calls, some 95 in all: reading the brief,
the plan and F0's section 8; reading the code 9; the program and the
tool written, to a build without warnings, 12; the records and the
first run of the scenarios, which passed, 6; the images, with the third
build, 16; the pattern's trial 4; the tool's own check, the records and
the documents the rest. Landing behind F4 and F7: the records
and the README's figures written anew, the section's lines on F7's
words in `copy.c` brought up to date, the suite again, and the images
held against those of origin's build, made in a copy under `build/`:
the same 37 differences in the same places. The change to the program is small: 185 lines
of `dos32.c`, 160 of `start.c`, 90 fewer in `read.c`, and the 22 places
of the bridge.

**What a sweep should do otherwise, F2 above all.**

- Save "before" first, and with the tool as it is at that commit. F1
  changed the tool and had to save a set again.
- A sweep moves nothing and changes no length, so its images are to be
  equal to the build's before with nothing declared but the four words
  that leave the main data, each by its `variable=` in `ADDRESSES`.
  Anything else that differs is a fault. No third build is needed
  where no layout changes; where one does, make the build that
  separates the layout from the code, as here.
- The bridge is as cheap as the plan thought: `SEG_OF(Room)` is exact
  and costs nothing to write. It is read anew at every use, which is
  what makes it safe with a room that may move; a sweep that keeps a
  panel's pointer in a variable is safe too, since a panel never moves
  from F1 on.
- The compiler holds a sweep both ways, tried with `wcc386 -wx -we`: a
  pointer handed where a number is taken and a number where a pointer
  is taken are W102, and a pointer held against a number is refused
  too. So F2 can go by a script and then by what the build refuses.
- What the plan feared most of F2, arithmetic on a panel and two
  panels held against each other by `<`, is gone with F1: it was all in
  `ReDr00`, `ReDr50`, `GiveMem` and `TakeMem`. What is left are twelve
  places that hold a panel against a word of the main data by `==` or
  `!=`, counted by `grep`, which are right of pointers.
- Count a table of the system's file in 32 bits: a `u16` index was six
  places for `portable_c-int16` to ask about. A difference of two
  pointers that is shifted is a place too, and wants its reason.
- `harness/dataimage.py check DIRECTORY` after any change to the tool.

**The pieces behind, from here.** Opinions, by what F1 cost.

- F2 is one agent's, if it goes by a script: its 496 places are of
  four patterns, and nothing in it needs thought once F1 has taken the
  arithmetic out. The reading is in the five places of kind i and in
  whatever held a panel under another name.
- F3 is the one to watch. It changes what `Dialog` and its like are
  handed in 21 files and teaches `harness/reads.py` a new form, and
  the test of the data judges it as well as the scenarios. If it is cut,
  then by `reads.py` first, alone, with the program unchanged.
- F4, F6, F7 and F8 look rightly sized. F4 and F6 meet the room: each
  takes `SEG_OF(Room)` out of its files and has `Room` itself.
- F5 is more than one agent holds, as the plan says: 29 `AT`, 24
  `AddressOf`, 21 `OFFSET_OF` and 13 `SEG_OF(Room)` in one file, and
  the arithmetic of `struct Address` is where C1's fault was. Cut it as
  the plan offers, `T50_00` to `T54_00` apart.
- F9 has less to do in the system's file than the plan has: the table
  of the blocks is there, and the tool reads it. It has `RoomParas`,
  `PANEL_BLOCK` and `ROOM_LEAST` to take out, 13 places.
### F2, a panel is a pointer: done, and what a later piece should know

A panel is a `struct WCBdef *` wherever it was a segment in a `u16`,
and `PANEL` is gone. All 155 scenarios pass with no golden and no patch
changed, at the first run of the swept build.

**What it is now.**

- Beside the main data, in `main.c`: `CurrentPanel`, `OtherPanel`,
  `LeftPanel` and `RightPanel`, which are `WCBcrn`, `WCBsec`, `WCB1seg`
  and `WCB2seg` of the original. The four words are in `struct MainDat`
  with "Not set or read here".
- Every `u16 panel` is a `struct WCBdef *panel`: 259 declarations, 88
  of them in `vc.h` and 171 in 19 files. `PANEL(x)` is `x`, 141 places.
  `InvWCB` answers with a panel. Three fields of structures are
  pointers: `ds` of `struct Regs`, the current panel as the main loop
  has it, and `panel` of `struct Onward` and of `struct Searched`.
- `MAIN_AS_PANEL` of `vc.h` is the main data where a panel is asked
  for, the five places of kind i, with one comment that says what is
  read so.
- A function that had `struct WCBdef *wcb = PANEL(panel);` had two
  names for one pointer once `PANEL` was gone. In 55 functions, where
  neither is set again, `wcb` went and the function says `panel`; 16
  keep both, where one of them is set again or `wcb` is declared apart
  from where it is set.

**How it was done.** A script of a hundred lines for the three
patterns, the four words, `PANEL(x)` and `u16 panel`, which wraps a
line that got too long at a comma and keeps a comment in its column;
then every file compiled by itself, so that one file's refusals do not
hide the next file's, 77 refusals the first time, which is the list of
what was read by hand. A second script for the second names.

**What was read by hand**, 44 places, and what each kind became:

| Kind | Places | What it became |
|---|---|---|
| The main data read as a panel, kind i | 5 | `MAIN_AS_PANEL`. `BegBX` of `place.c` reads nothing of the panel that it is handed: it holds the pointer against the left panel, and the main data is not that. So the two calls of `BegBX`, in `Init40` of `main.c` and `F16_00` of `keys.c`, and `PutPrm` of `bars.c`, called by `F21_31` of `enter.c`, read no byte of the main data so. `M60_02` of `commands.c` reads `Visible`, byte 2, and `ReDr00` of `read.c` `WinPath[3]`, byte 23: both are of `ColTab`, in the first 82 bytes, as the plan took it |
| A panel under another name | 13 | `other` in `commands.c`, three times, in `info.c`, `keys.c` and `read.c`, `current` in `commands.c` and `keys.c`, `left` in `keys.c`, and `panel` in a list of names in `find.c` and `main.c`: each a `struct WCBdef *`. `other` of `copy.c` went, its one use being a line. `i` of `F20_02` in `keys.c`, which held the other panel for three lines: those say `other`, which the function has from its first line and nothing changes between |
| A register of the main loop | 1 | `r->di` in `F39_01` of `main.c`, where the original has the segment of the menu's panel in DI: not set any more, with the reason at the place. Nothing reads DI as a menu leaves it: the three commands that take it are the mouse's, which `Loop` asks for with DI set, and no table of a menu has one of them |
| A panel's segment kept in a word of a buffer | 2 | `OWNER` of `tree.c`, a word of `MenuBuf` at 48 with the path behind it at 50: it stays a segment, `SEG_OF(panel)` where it is set and `SEG_OF(CurrentPanel)` where it is held against the current panel. F7 has `tree.c` |
| A panel handed on as the segment that something is in | 8 | `SEG_OF(panel)`: the fifth argument of `Dialog`, four calls in `commands.c` and one in `enter.c`, and `segment != SEG_OF(LeftPanel)` in `Dialog` itself, which are F3's; `segment` of `Run_00` in `usermenu.c`, for `ClsLine`, F3's too; `segment` of `F77_10` in `cmdline.c`, the list that the speed search goes through, a panel's or the tree's, which is F7's |
| An offset in a panel's segment reckoned with | 2 | In `F23_02` of `enter.c` two offsets of one path were held against each other: two pointers into that path are now. In `PutInf` of `info.c` the offset of an entry is held against `EndBuf`: `(u16)((const u8 *)file - (const u8 *)other)`, the number that it was |
| Where a panel is made | 1 | `Init11` of `start.c`: `(struct WCBdef *)AT(block.value, 0)`, of the segment that `MemTake` answers with. F9's |
| Two panels held against each other | 12 | All by `==` or `!=`, as F1 counted: right of pointers, and left as they were |

Nothing of it changes what DOS is handed. No function of `sys.h` took
a panel as a number: the compiler would have refused the call, and
refused none. The rows of entry 6 of `DEVIATIONS.md` that speak of DS
on a panel's segment say what the original has there; the functions
have DS on the main data, before and after.

**What the compiler does not refuse**, and was looked for by `grep`:

- A pointer handed to a word of `vc.h` that casts what it is handed,
  `AT(panel, 0)`, `OFFSET_IN_SEG(panel, x)`: the cast makes a number
  of the pointer with no word said. There were four, all read.
- `u16 panel, size, drive;` made `struct WCBdef *panel, size, drive;`
  by a script declares structures. The compiler refused the one there
  was, by what was assigned to them; one that is never assigned would
  be 6,754 bytes of the stack.
- A pointer that is stepped, added to or held against another by `<`:
  none.

**The image.** `compare` of the build before, saved before anything
was changed, with the piece's build: "155 scenarios, 0 with nothing
that differs; 6 differences, 0 more in what was declared as changed,
883 in what may differ", and "313 pointers that name the same in
both". The four words are held by what they name, each by its
`variable=` in `ADDRESSES`, and nothing was declared as changed. No
panel differs, nothing behind the panels, no byte of the main data but
the six. What differed at first was 732 bytes of three kinds, each of
which follows the build with no fault in either, and each is in the
tool now with its reason, which the session has approved:

- `dos32.OwnBlocks`, in every scenario: the paragraphs that the blocks
  begin in, one further on, since the four pointers are 16 bytes of
  `_BSS` in front of the 640 KB. The linker's maps say that nothing
  else of the data moved: the main data and everything in front of
  `_BSS` are where they were, the code being 459 bytes shorter and
  within the same page.
- `dos32.Below`, in 152 scenarios: the stack pointer at the last call
  of DOS, 468 bytes further down. See "The stack" below.
- `DTA+41`, in 108 scenarios, 95h before and 91h after, and the six
  that are left: the same byte where the program has copied a name as
  13 bytes, in `TmpBuf` and `TmpErr` of `copy` and `copy-dirs`. The
  record of a search comes up from DOS's memory, and behind a name of
  fewer than twelve characters is what that memory held before the
  program was handed it. What was seen: at 6E24h the two files have
  95h and 91h, in the table that says where the relocations of each
  page begin, and that is the one place where the two files have those
  two bytes at the same offset; and this build has fewer relocations,
  since `PANEL` named `md`. What is inferred, and was not looked at in
  DOS's memory: that the byte is one of the program's own file, as the
  extender read it to load it. **Every piece that changes the code
  may move this byte**: where a difference is a pair of bytes that
  `DTA+41` has too, it is this. Whoever wants it shown and not
  inferred: a build that differs from another in its relocations and
  in nothing that runs, a function that nothing calls with a few
  addresses in it, and the two builds' images.

No variant was built: the layout differs in one known thing, and the
three kinds are each one value in every scenario.

The tool, besides: a word's variable is held by what it names and no
longer as bytes too (`POINTERS`), so a pointer that names another
place is one difference and not two, and "pointers that name the same"
counts each once; and `check` changes its byte of a word where the
build has the word, and of a variable that two builds are held to have
alike. `check` catches each of its nine bytes in the images of the
build before and of this one.

**The stack.** `struct Onward` is a pointer, a byte and a byte: eight
bytes where it was four, so it comes back through a pointer to room in
the caller's frame, and `wcc386` gives every call its own room.
`Command` of `main.c` calls some fifty commands that return one: its
frame is 396 bytes where it was 12. The least that a scenario leaves of
the stack is 14,410 of 16,384 bytes. A variable that the calls share
would take it back, in N16 or whenever `Command` is next read.

**The records.** The words that were F2's are at nothing: `u16 panel`
259, `PANEL` 141, `md.WCBcrn` 42, `md.WCB1seg` 23, `md.WCB2seg` 20,
`md.WCBsec` 11. `SEG_OF` is up by 10 to 34, `OFFSET_IN_SEG` down by 4
to 4, `MAIN_SEG` down by 4 to 73, and `MAIN_AS_PANEL` is new, 5 places,
and stays. Left to go: F3 277, F5 45, F6 44, F7 67, F8 212, F9 13, F10
213. The record of the widths has 150 numbers fewer and one cut more:
by file, the 135 `u16 panel` that a file writes and not only declares,
the 12 under other names, and the three fields, held against the
record's rows file for file; the cut is the cast of `info.c`. The host
check's record and that of `portable_c-int16` did not move.

**A number that the piece added.** One: in `PutInf` of `info.c` the
offset of an entry in the other panel, `(u16)((const u8 *)file - (const
u8 *)other)`, a difference of two pointers cut to 16 bits and without
a sign, held against `EndBuf`. It is what `OFFSET_IN_SEG` gave there
and is left so, an offset in a panel being 16 bits for as long as
`EndBuf` is: N12, which has `info.c`, sorts it with the rest of the
file, by the rule for a number and for its sign. Nothing else that the
piece wrote is a number: what it changed became pointers.

**As it landed.** Rebased onto `c4e1c06`, behind the four names taken
out of `sys.h` and the record of the widths in its new form, which was
written anew and read again file for file: the same 150 numbers and
the one cut. The program is the same bytes as before the rebase, and
that of `c4e1c06` the same as the build that the piece started from.
Its images, saved anew, against the piece's: "155 scenarios, 0 with
nothing that differs; 6 differences, 0 more in what was declared as
changed, 883 in what may differ", the same six.

**How long it took**, in tool calls, some 105: reading 14; the script
and what the compiler refused, to a clean build, 22; the records 6; the
images, with what the three kinds were, 14; the second names 3; the
tool's check 4; the documents and the rest.

**F3, from here.** Opinions.

- It is larger than F2 in thought, and cut in two it is two pieces of
  F2's size. What a dialog's fields are in, the last argument of
  `Dialog`, `ClsLine` and their like, a panel or the main data: that is
  F2 again, 73 `MAIN_SEG` and the eight `SEG_OF` of this piece, a
  script and the compiler. What a table is handed as, `OFFSET`,
  `AsmSeg`, `NAMED`, 277 places, is the other, and has
  `harness/reads.py` to teach first, with the program unchanged, as
  F1 said.
- The compiler holds less of it than of F2. A box is a structure of
  its own type, so whatever takes any box takes a `const void *` or a
  `const u8 *`, and anything is handed to that without a word. And
  `OFFSET` is reckoned with where `PANEL` never was: `OFFSET(Menu_T) +
  (table - 1) * sizeof *Menu_T` in `F39_01`, `r->si` and `r->di` of the
  main loop holding a table's offset, `OFFSET(AltSr_T) + i`. Those are
  read, not swept.
- A structure that is returned and grows over four bytes costs the
  caller's frame a room for every call: look at the frames in the
  listings, `enter` at a function's first line, if one does.
- Any change of the code moves `DTA+41`; see above.

### F3a, what a dialog's fields are in: done, and what the second half should know

The first half of F3, as F2 cut it. Where a routine was handed the
segment that a dialog's fields, the texts that a box puts in or the
colour of a line are in, it is handed a pointer to that thing, and
reads at the offset that the table names. All 155 scenarios pass with
no golden and no patch changed, at the first run of the swept build.

**What it is now.**

- `Dialog(box, include, begin, saved, void *data)` and `DialBox(place,
  box, include, const void *data, where)`, with `DiBx30` behind the
  second: `data` is `&md`, or a panel. A line to type into is read and
  written at `(u8 *)data + field->mPoint`, a box to tick at `(u8 *)data
  + NUMBER_OF(field->mCtrl)`, a text that a box puts in at `(const u8
  *)data + entry->from`. The offsets in the tables are as they were,
  `MD_AT`, `WCB_AT` and `NUMBER`, and no table changed. What a field
  keeps in the main data whatever it is handed, the line chosen, a tick
  while the dialog is up, the button, is read by `MD` as before.
- "Of a panel: in the half of the screen that the panel has" is `data
  != LeftPanel` in `Dialog`, two pointers held against each other by
  `!=`.
- `ClsLine(place, const struct MainDat *data)` reads `data->CrntCol`,
  where it read the byte at `CrntCol`'s offset in a segment.
- `PANEL_AS_MAIN(panel)` of `vc.h` is a panel where the main data is
  asked for, `MAIN_AS_PANEL` the other way round, and it has one place:
  `Run_00` of `usermenu.c` comes to `ClsLine` with DS left on the
  current panel when the commands have no room for a name, and the
  colour of the line is then the byte of the panel that is as far into
  it as `CrntCol` is into the main data, AB8h, which is within
  `struct WCBdef`. The word is named in
  `WORDS` of `harness/int16.py` and of `harness/words.py`, where it
  stays, as `MAIN_AS_PANEL` does: it rests on the two layouts, not on
  the megabyte.
- `MAIN_SEG` has four places left in the code, none of them a
  dialog's: `V82_00(MAIN_SEG, ...)` in `view.c`, where a search looks
  through `MenuBuf` and not through the viewer's text, which is F4's;
  `T72_00(line, MAIN_SEG, ...)` in `edit.c`, a line of the editor that
  is in the main data, F5's; and the list that the speed search goes
  through, `Search(MAIN_SEG, ...)` in `treebox.c` and `segment =
  MAIN_SEG` in `cmdline.c`, F7's, with `segment = SEG_OF(panel)` beside
  the second, which F2 left to F7 already. Its definition goes with
  F10, as the record has it.

**How it was done.** A script of sixty lines, `build/f3a-sweep.py`, not
kept: it reads each call of `Dialog`, `DialBox` and `ClsLine` from its
name to the bracket that closes it, over as many lines as the call has,
and takes the argument at the place of the segment where that is
`MAIN_SEG` or `SEG_OF(panel)` and nothing else. Then the three
functions by hand, and every file compiled by itself. The compiler
refused nothing: every call had the one or the other written out.

| | Places | What it became |
|---|---|---|
| By the script: `Dialog(..., MAIN_SEG)` | 55 in 15 files, the `Ask` of `copy.c` among them, which is a macro around one | `&md` |
| By the script: `DialBox(..., MAIN_SEG, ...)` | 8 in 6 files | `&md` |
| By the script: `ClsLine(..., MAIN_SEG)` | 4 in 3 files | `&md` |
| By the script: `Dialog(..., SEG_OF(panel))` | 5, four in `commands.c` and one in `enter.c` | `panel` |
| By hand: the three functions and `DiBx30` | 4 signatures, 3 prototypes of `vc.h`, 3 calls that hand `segment` on, and 5 reads through `AT(segment, ...)` in `dialog.c` | A pointer and a number added to it, as above |
| By hand: the comparison in `Dialog` | 1 | `data != LeftPanel` |
| By hand: `ClsLine` | 1 read | `data->CrntCol` |
| By hand: `segment` of `Run_00` in `usermenu.c` | 4 lines: the variable, two assignments of `MAIN_SEG` and one of `SEG_OF(CurrentPanel)`, and the call | `const struct MainDat *data`, `&md` and `PANEL_AS_MAIN(CurrentPanel)` |
| By a second script: a call's last line that held `&md)` or `panel)` alone | 6 | Joined to the line before, where the whole fits |
| Comments | 9, in `dialog.c`, `bars.c`, `vc.h` and `commands.c` | Say `data` and what it is, where they said `segment` and `MAIN_SEG` |

Of the five calls that hand a panel, one means it: the filter's
dialog, `Filt_B`, whose line and two ticks are named by `WCB_AT`. The
other four are the original with DS left on the panel, in `F30_00` of

`Quit_B`, `CmpDi_B`, `SvSt_B` and `SetEr_B` have buttons and nothing
else, their boxes put no text in, and none has the menu of a panel, so

written there, since nothing of the main data is read in the panel.
And the main data is handed to no dialog that names a field of a
panel: `Filt_B` has one call.

**What the compiler does not refuse**, and how it was looked at:

- `void *` takes any pointer. A script of fifteen lines tallied what
  each call hands, by the same reading of a call: `Dialog` 55 times
  `&md` and 5 times `panel`, `DialBox` 8 times `&md` and once `data`,
  from `Dialog`, `ClsLine` 4 times `&md` and once `data`, in `Run_00`.
  `ClsLine` is typed, so a panel handed to it without the word is
  refused.
- A 0 is a pointer to nothing to the compiler, and `Dialog` has two
  zeros in front of `data` at most of its calls. No call has a number
  where `data` is: the tally has every one.
- `AT(data, x)` would have made a segment of a pointer without a word:
  the five `AT(segment, ...)` were each rewritten by hand, and
  `dialog.c` has no `AT` left but those of the tables, `AT(code, ...)`,
  13 of them, which are the second half's.

**A number cut where it was cut.** `AT` cut the offset that it was
handed to 16 bits. What is added to `data` now is a `u16` by its type
at each of the six places, `mPoint` and `from` of `tables.h` and what
`NUMBER_OF` answers, so nothing is cut that was not, and no cast was
written. No number was added by the piece.

**The image.** `compare` of the build before, saved before anything
was changed, with the piece's build: "155 scenarios, 46 with nothing
that differs; 6 differences, 0 more in what was declared as changed,
132 in what may differ", and "464 pointers that name the same in
both". Nothing was declared as changed, and nothing of the main data
changed its home. The six are F2's six, in `copy` and `copy-dirs`, the
byte behind a name that was copied as 13 bytes into `TmpBuf` and

108 scenarios where the tool knows it, the same pair. The other 24 of
what may differ are `dos32.Below`, the stack pointer at the last call
of DOS. No panel differs, nothing of the room, no pattern round a
block.

**The program.** Its code is 169 bytes shorter and its file 476 bytes
longer, 306,611 where it was 306,135, for 71 addresses more that the
extender sets, 5,196 where there were 5,125: `&md` is an address where
`MAIN_SEG` was a number. The table of the README has what it is now.

**The records.** The words that were this half's: `MAIN_SEG` 73 in 18
files before and 4 in 4 after, its definition besides; `SEG_OF` 34 in 13
and 27 in 9, the five of `Dialog`, that of the comparison and that of

F10 213. The table of the words says of `MAIN_SEG` and of `u16
segment` what is left of each and whose it is; no count moved from one

no cut more or fewer: the three `segment` of `dialog.c`, `ClsLine`'s
in `bars.c` and that of `Run_00` in `usermenu.c`, each a parameter or
a variable that is a pointer now. The host check's record and that of
`portable_c-int16` did not move.

**As it landed.** Rebased onto `7ebaec0`, behind the five leaf files'
numbers with a sign and the record of the widths in its new form,
which was taken as it stood and written anew: the same five numbers
gone and nothing else. The figures of "The program" above are of the
build before the rebase; as it landed the file is 306,603 bytes where
that of `7ebaec0` is 306,151, 452 more, its code 169 bytes shorter,
and the addresses 5,196 for 5,125. The whole suite passes, 13 tests.
The images of `7ebaec0`, built in a copy and saved anew, against the
piece's: "155 scenarios, 46 with nothing that differs; 6 differences,
0 more in what was declared as changed, 109 in what may differ", the

**How long it took**, in tool calls, some 60: reading the plan and
the three sections 9; the script, the three functions and a clean
compile 12; the records 5; the images and the suite 10, most of them

the calls were all of one form.

**The second half, from here.** What a table is handed as.

- `include` of `Dialog` is two things. It is the text that ^I stands
  for, an offset in the tables' segment or 0 for none; and for a
  dialog whose box is on the screen already, `BOX_THERE`, it is the
  size of that box, with `begin` and `saved` where the box is and what
  it covers: `Dialog` has `u16 size = include;` at its top. Three
  calls hand a size there, two in `edit.c`, `BigFi_B` and `NewFi_B`,
  and one in `find.c`, `Find_B`. A pointer cannot be both: either
  `Dialog` gets a parameter for the size, which is three calls changed
  and 57 with one more zero, or those three go to a second function
  that takes the box as it is on the screen.
- `include` is not always a table's. In `FtErr1` of `main.c` it is
  `OFFSET_IN_SEG(assembly, text)`, a text that is the device driver's
  name or a line of the main data, made an offset in the tables'
  segment: a pointer says it as it is.
- Once `box` and `include` are pointers too, `Dialog` is handed three
  pointers and two numbers, and the compiler takes a 0 for any of
  them and any pointer for a `const void *`. A box is a structure of
  its own type, as F2 said; what would hold the order is `include` as
  `const u8 *`, which a box is refused for, and the box as `const
  struct BOXHD *` with the cast in a word at the call, or the tally
  above run again: it is fifteen lines and reads every call.
- `first = box + sizeof(struct BOXHD)` and `FIELD(item)` in `Dialog`
  step through the fields by an offset in the tables' segment, and
  `MinMnu`, `MnMn10` and `MnMn40` are handed `control`, `colors` and
  `table` so: those are reckoned with, not only handed on.
- What a dialog's fields are in is done, so the second half changes no
  `data` and no `&md`: of a call's five arguments the first two are
  its own.
- The four calls that hand a panel where nothing reads it, above, are
  as the original has DS. Nothing asks that they stay so but the
  comments at them.
- `Search` of `input.c` and its two callers are F7's, `V82_00`'s
  `MAIN_SEG` F4's and `T72_00`'s F5's, as above: each is the main data
  where a text or a list is looked through, and `(u8 *)&md` when the
  text is a `u8 *`.
- Any change of the code moves `DTA+41` in the images: F2's section,
  "The image".

### F3b, what a table is handed as: done, and what F4 to F8 should know

The second half of F3. A box, a dialog, a text, a line of buttons and a
table of colours are handed on by a pointer, where each was handed on
as its offset in the segment of the tables: `OFFSET`, `AsmSeg`,
`TABLES_BY` and `NAMED` are gone from the tree, 277 places by the
words' record. All 155 scenarios pass with no golden and no patch
changed, at the first run of the swept build; the whole suite passes,
13 tests.

**What it is now.**

- A file of code declares a table as what it hands on. A text, buttons
  and colours are `extern const u8 Name[];`, as they were, and are
  named `Name`, or `Name + 1`. A box is declared as what every box
  begins with, `extern const struct BOXTOP Name;`, and a dialog as its
  header, `extern const struct BOXHD Name;`, and each is handed on as
  `&Name`. `vc.h` declares the two structures by their tags, so a file
  of code needs no `tables.h`. This is what F3's row left to decide,
  "what a table is typed as where it is handed on": a file of code sees
  neither how many lines a box has nor its fields, and the compiler
  holds a box, a dialog and a text apart at every call, which the
  names do not: `Copy1_B` is a dialog and `OpnEr_B` one too, `CopFi_P`
  a box, `Copy1_P` a box that only a table names.
- `DialBox(place, const struct BOXTOP *head, const u8 *include, data,
  where)`, `OncZoom` the same, `Dialog(const struct BOXHD *head, const
  u8 *include, begin, size, data)`, `MinMnu(const u8 *control, begin,
  size, const u8 *color, keys, item)`, `MnMn10` and `MnMn40` with
  `const u8 *table`. A word of a table that names something is read as
  the pointer that it is: `*line`, `head->pDiBox`, `field->mCtrl`,
  `picture->page`.
- `Dialog`'s fourth parameter is `size`, where it was `saved`. F3a had
  three calls that hand a size as `include`; it is one. `Find_B` of
  `find.c` is the only dialog with `BOX_THERE`, and hands `begin` and
  `size`. `BigFi_B` and `NewFi_B` of `edit.c` have no such flag: the
  assembly leaves in DX, BX and SI what the box before had there, the
  two boxes have no `^I`, and a dialog that puts its box up reads
  neither `begin` nor a size, so the two calls hand zeros and their
  comment says so. `saved` was never read as it came: `Dialog` sets it
  from `DialBox` for a box that it puts up and reads it for no other.
  So it went, and with it the fourth parameter of `T00_00`, which had
  no reader left.
- `include` is a pointer, 0 for none, and where the original has DX on
  a text of the main data it is that text: `text` in `FtErr1`,
  `md.TmpBuf` and `md.MenuBuf` in `Run_00` of `usermenu.c`, `md.TmpBuf`
  in `Aexec0` of `view.c`. The last three boxes have no `^I`, so
  nothing reads it; the C had the place of the main data there as an
  offset among the tables, which named nothing.

**How it was done.** `harness/reads.py` first, in a commit of its own
with the program unchanged, tried on a copy of the tree that a script
had swept: the tool printed of the copy, which did not compile, line
for line what it printed of the tree. Then the script on the tree,
`build/f3b/sweep.py`, seventy lines and not kept; `vc.h` and `misc.c`
with the four words taken out, so that the compiler refuses every use
that is left; and each file compiled by itself until it was taken.

| | Places | What it became |
|---|---|---|
| By the script: a box or a dialog declared | 93 declarations in 17 files, of the 151 boxes and dialogs that the files of tables have | `extern const struct BOXTOP Name;`, `extern const struct BOXHD Name;` |
| By the script: `OFFSET(Name)` of a box or a dialog | 108 | `&Name` |
| By the script: `OFFSET(Name)` of bytes | 85 | `Name` |
| By the script: `AT(code, OFFSET(Name) + n)`, with `assembly` and `AsmSeg()` for `code` | 37 | `Name + n`, in brackets where it is read through |
| By hand, the compiler naming each: a variable that held the offset | Some twenty, in 9 files: `include` 7 times, `report` 3, `box` 3, `shown` 2, `title` 2, `words`, `file`, `reason`, `control` | `const u8 *`, `const struct BOXHD *`, `const struct BOXTOP *` |
| By hand, the compiler naming each: a function that took or returned the offset | 20: the six of `vc.h` and `MnMn11`, `MnMn41`, `MnMn50`, `MnMn60`, `Dial85` behind them, `F35_40`, `Masked`, `M64_02`, `F10_01`, `F47_01`, `FncMas`, `FncMs1`, `V80_00`, `T76_00` | The same |
| By hand: `AsmSeg`, 29 places by the record | The variable `code` or `assembly` that kept it, in 13 functions, where the compiler said that nothing reads it any more; the function and its prototype; the others stood in an `AT` that the script took | Gone |
| By hand: `NAMED(word)` | 15, eleven in `dialog.c`, three in `stcolor.c`, one in `main.c` | The pointer itself |
| By hand: comments that said "by their offsets in the segment that AsmSeg returns" | Some thirty-five, in 22 files, found by `grep` for `AsmSeg` and for `offset` | Say what is handed on |

**The places that reckon**, each read:

| Where | What it was | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `Dialog`: `first = box + sizeof(struct BOXHD)` | An offset behind the header | A pointer: `(const struct BOXMN *)(head + 1)` |
| `Dialog`: `item` and `cursor`, with `FIELD(offset)` | Offsets stepped by `sizeof(struct BOXMN)` | Pointers to a field, stepped by `++` and `--`; `FIELD` is gone |
| `Dialog`: `(u16)(cursor - sizeof(struct BOXMN)) >= first` | Two offsets held against each other | `cursor > first`: the cursor is never in front of the first field |
| `Dialog`: `first + (link & LINK_FIELD) * sizeof(struct BOXMN)` | An offset reckoned | An index into the fields: `first + (link & LINK_FIELD)` |
| `Dial85` | Stepped an offset to the last field | Steps a pointer and returns one |
| `MnMn11`: `for (item = table; ; item += 2)`, twice, and `item - table >> 1`, twice | An offset stepped through the buttons, and how far it got | `button` stepped, and a difference of two pointers into one line of buttons, `(u16)(button - table >> 1)` |
| `MnMn50`, `MnMn41`: `AT(code, table + n)` | An offset reckoned | An index, `table[n]`, and `table + count` |
| `MinMnu`: `colors`, an offset | Read as three bytes | `const u8 *color`; `Dialog` hands it the colours of its box, `((const struct BOXTOP *)head->pDiBox)->colors` |
| `F39_01` of `main.c`: `OFFSET(Menu_T) + (table - 1) * sizeof *Menu_T`, and the command at `r->si + r->bx` | Two offsets reckoned, and SI set to the table | Two indexes: `Menu_T[table - 1][r->bx >> 1]`. BX is twice the place of the item, below 256 and even, since `F39_00` names a table only with an item chosen, 1 to 254. `r->si` is not set: nothing reads SI as a menu leaves it, as F2 found of DI |
| `Loop` of `main.c`: `r->di = OFFSET(AltSr_T) + i` | DI behind the key found in the table | Not set, with a comment: `F77_00` takes the key alone, and the three commands that take DI are the mouse's, which `Loop` asks for with DI set |
| `F35_50` of `copy.c`: `*AT(AsmSeg(), title + i)` and `words + i` | Offsets read at an index | `title[i]`, `words[i]` |
| `copy.c`: the macro `ASM(object, offset)`, two places | A pointer made of an offset and a number | `CopFi_S[12 + i]`, `CopTo_S[2 + i]`; the tool knows both by their form now, with the counts that `REVIEWED` had |
| `T00_00` of `edit.c`: `line.include = AT(code, 76)` | What the assembly leaves in DX, taken for an offset | 0: none of the lines has `^I`, and 76 names no text |
| `T00_00`: `OFFSET_IN_SEG(code, line.line)` | A pointer made an offset to hand on | `line.line` |
| `F38_00` of `dirfunc.c`: `include = selected.files` | The number of files selected, as the assembly has DX, taken for an offset | 0, with the comment that was there: the box has no `^I` |

**What the compiler refused, and what it does not.**

- With `-we` a number where a pointer is asked for stops the build, and
  so does a pointer kept in a `u16`: every variable and parameter of the
  table above was named by W102 or W126, and so was each of two
  variables that held now a box and now a dialog. `report` of two
  functions of `copy.c` was first the box that says what is copied and
  then the dialog of an error, and `result` of a third the box and then
  a number: the box has a variable of its own there now, `shown`.
- It does not refuse a 0 for a pointer, nor any pointer for the two
  words of a table that are `const void *`, `pDiBox` and `mCtrl`. A
  script of a hundred lines, `build/f3b/tally.py`, not kept, read every
  call as F3a's did and the files of tables besides: each of the 97
  calls of `Dialog`, 17 of them through `Ask` of `copy.c`, of `DialBox`
  and of `OncZoom` hands a dialog or a box as it is asked; no box whose
  lines have `^I` is handed 0; and three calls hand a text to a box
  that has no `^I`, `NoEmp_B` in `dirfunc.c`, `UsrEr_B` in `usermenu.c`
  and the box of `Aexec0`.
- The script wrote wrong C in two places, where an offset was reckoned
  with inside the brackets: `F39_01`, and the macro `ASM`. Both are in
  the table above, and both were refused or read before anything ran.

**The tool of the reads.** `harness/reads.py` knows a table that is
handed on in either form, the C translation keeping the first for
good: `Name` and `&Name` as an argument of a routine of `READERS`, or
kept in `box`, `report`, `result` or `shown` for one; `== &Name` and

equal to those of the commit that the piece started from, with nothing
declared. Two commits: a bug of the original that the switch to 32
bits had fixed unasked, declared as fixed on the user's word, and the
sweep.

It is not the reckoning of a segment and an offset: the piece takes

for every byte that it looks at, `UpCase` asks `CaseMap` of the

`CaseMap` of `dos32.c` calls DOS's routine for capitals in real mode,
through the extender, DPMI 0301h: into real mode and back for every
byte of the text, some 320 instructions each, where the original and
the C translation make a far call. The last column shows it: the
piece's source of before F3b with eleven lines more in `CaseMap`,
which keep what DOS answered for a letter and ask for each letter
once. The step is then shorter than the original's. That was a trial
in `build/` and is not in the tree.

The mend is not of the addresses and is not made, and will not be:
**the user has decided, on 13 October 2026, that the search stays as
slow as it is** (`CLAUDE.md`, "The portable C"). Every byte's capital
is asked of DOS through the extender as the original asks it, and
remembering the answers was offered and not taken. Nothing changes in
`dos32.c`. What was offered, for the record, two ways, both of which
change what DOS is asked and when:

- The system's file remembers what DOS's routine answered for a
  letter, and forgets it when the country is asked for again, which
  the program does when it starts and after every command, in
  `IniData`. DOS's routine is then called
  once for each letter that the program meets, 256 times at the most
  between two commands, and the answers are DOS's own. It takes for
  granted that the routine answers the same for the same letter until
  the country is asked for again, which it does in every DOS that is
  known, being a table.
- `UpCase` asks only for a byte of 80h or more, which is what the
  routine is documented for. That is common code doing otherwise than
  the original for the bytes below, where a DOS could answer anything,
  and it leaves a text of Russian as slow as it is.

The first was the one recommended. With it `view-search` and `find`
would end at some 1.15 times the original's clock where they end at
twice.

### F7, the tree, the history, the commands: done but for the commands of a line, and what a later piece should know

The five words of the main data that kept a place of it are pointers
beside it, the tree's list is a pointer, and what F2 and F3a left to
this piece is done. The lines of a menu file and of an extension file,
which are places of `MenuBuf` in `u16` from `FndItem` to `Run_00`, are
left: they run through `view.c`, which F4 has. The whole suite passes,
14 tests, with all 155 scenarios and no golden and no patch changed, at
the first run.

**What it is now.**

- Beside the main data, in `main.c`: `TreeCursor`, `TreeFirst` and
  `TreeCurrent`, each a `struct DIRENT *`, `HistoryPlace`, a `const u8
  *`, and `NextCommand`, a `u8 *`. They are `TreAdr`, `TreFrst`,
  `TreCrnt`, `HstAdr` and `BatAdr` of the original; the five words are
  in `struct MainDat` with "Not set or read here". `TreeCurrent` is 0
  where the word was 0, for none.
- `TRELIST` is the pointer to the list's first entry, where it was that
  entry's place: `TRELIST + n`, `entry - TRELIST`, `entry >= TreeFirst`.
- Where one routine moves a cursor through a panel's files or through
  the tree alike, an entry of the tree is an offset in the tree's list,
  in bytes and in 16 bits, as a file is an offset in its panel:
  `TREE_OFFSET(entry)` and `TREE_ENTRY(offset)` of `vc.h`, which stay.
  That is `struct Shown` with `ChgAdr` and `NumAdr` of `place.c`,
  `F00_50` of `keys.c`, the speed search, and the tree's box,
  `ChTree`. The original has the entry's place of the main data there.
  The two differ by where the list begins, in every such number alike.

- N11. `struct Shown`, `ChgAdr` and `NumAdr` of `place.c` carry an

- N13. `ChTree`'s six variables above are the ones that count on

  numbers of entries with a sign, and then `ChTr50` with them, which

  cast when `n` is widened. `TreeCursor` and `TreeFirst` stand two
  entries further on than they are for a moment in `ChTree`, which is

- N15. `Search` steps `at` by `step` and wraps it to `begin` at `end`,

- N17a, of `keys.c`: `first` and `cursor` of `F00_50` are such offsets

### F6, a copy and what goes through files: done, and what a later piece should know

The piece F6, in `copy.c` and `dirfunc.c`, in two commits: `NEAR` out
of both files, with `VC.EXE` the same bytes; then a copy's buffer as a
pointer into the room, and the two words of `TmpBuf` that held an
address taken out. All 155 scenarios pass with no golden and no patch
changed, and the whole suite, 14 tests.

**What it is now.**

- `C20_00` keeps a pointer, `buffer`, where it was in the room, and
  reads into `buffer + offset` and writes from `buffer`. Its steps are
  the assembly's: 32K behind each piece that is read, whatever was
  read; behind a piece that is written as many whole paragraphs as
  were written, `got >> 4 << 4`, which leaves out what is beyond a
  paragraph as the assembly does and stays right for a `got` that is
  made wider. Nothing of it wrapped: the offset is 8000h at most, and
  the room ended below A000h paragraphs.
- CpCont, the word at `TmpBuf+128` that said where to go on after a
  full disk, is `rest`, a variable of `C20_00`: that routine alone sets
  and reads it, cleared for each file as the word was, and it is not
  kept across anything that moves the room.
- CpBgNam, the word at `TmpBuf+102` that held the place where the name
  begins in the source's path, is a static pointer of `copy.c`, set by
  the commands and read for each file. The bytes of the two words are
  not set or read by the file, and a comment at the macros says so.
- `NEAR` is gone from both files, 38 places. At 27 what it was handed
  is a `u8 *`, or it is kept in a pointer to `const`. At 11, and 2 more
  where CpBgNam is set, it took `const` off what `CutPath` answers, for
  a name in a buffer of the program's own that is then written: those
  say `(u8 *)CutPath(...)`, as `C20_00` said it of `C00_End` already.
  `CutPath` takes and answers a pointer to `const`, as `strchr` does in
  C, and a caller that writes there says so.

| A segment kept in a word of the main data | CpCont, set by a sum of paragraphs and held against 0 | `rest`, a pointer, 0 for none |

**N9, from here** (`copy.c`):

- `left` is a `u32` of bytes, `(u32)(RoomParas() & 0xFFE0) << 4`: the

  that DOS is asked for; S makes what `FileRead` and `FileWrite` take
  and answer an `i32`. Where `got` is widened, `got >> 4 << 4` stays
  right; a mask in its place would want writing anew.
- Nothing bounds how far a read goes into the room but `left`, and for
  a device that gives a piece in several calls `left` is counted down
  by the last call alone while `buffer` goes on 32K: "Known and not
  dealt with" has it, by reading. A read then runs behind the room's
  end, as it ran behind it in the 640 KB, and from F9 on the extender
  ends the program for that, "What could go wrong", 14. For a file it
  cannot happen: a piece is read whole or the file has ended. This is
  what N9 says when it writes how it knows that nothing writes behind
  the block's end, and whether it is to be mended is the user's.
  (Mended, on the user's word: entry 17 of `DEVIATIONS.md`, and "N9,
  `copy.c`" below.)
- The short write on a full disk, the 15 bytes written twice, is the
  same entry of "Known and not dealt with", and `got >> 4 << 4` is it.
- `count = to - CpDest` of `C00_01` is a difference of two pointers
  into `CpDest` kept in a `u16`: signed by nature, and within the 81
  bytes of `CpDest`.
- `rest` and CpBgNam are pointers now and no number to sort.

### F5, the editor: done, and what a later piece should know

The text of the editor is `Room`, a `u8 *`, and a place in it a number
added to it: `AddressOf`, `OFFSET_OF`, `struct Address` and `T62_00`
are gone, with every `AT`, `SEG_OF(Room)`, `u16 segment`, `MAIN_SEG`,
`MD_POINTER` and `NEAR` of `edit.c`. All 155 scenarios pass with no
golden and no patch changed, and the whole suite, 14 tests. Nothing of
`vc.h` changed, nor a caller in another file.

**The cut.** None was made: the piece is one commit. The cut that the
plan offered, `T50_00` to `T54_00` apart, does not cut: `struct Where`
is what every key that moves the cursor hands to `T53_00` and `T54_00`,
so the two halves meet in some twenty functions. What made the whole
small enough is that the text could be read as places only, which the
next paragraph says, and that what was left is a few lines each.

**Where a segment was stepped to keep an offset small**, each read,
and each held against the old code on this computer (below):

| Where | What the assembly does by the segment | What it is now |
|---|---|---|
| `T53_10` | Looks no further than 0FFFEh of the segment of the address that it is given, and has no end for a line that goes on; in hex, none where the offset wraps | Looks as far as the text goes. Every caller either asked again, from the address with the lowest offset and then a piece of 0FF00h bytes on at a time (`T53_00`, `T00_20`), which finds the same two characters, or took such a line for one longer than the buffer keeps, 3,900, which it is (`T50_00`) |
| `T53_00` | A line that does not end in the segment of its address, looked at again from the address made anew, and then a piece at a time; the address that comes back is in the segment it was given, offsets growing down the window | `where->place = end.at`. Which segment an address had changed nothing that it answered |
| `T54_00` | Back through at most 32K at a time, taking a lower segment; in hex `segment - 1`, and no line before one in the first segment | A place counted down, `at`, an `i32` since from the second byte of the text it is the byte before; in hex `place - 16`, and none for a place below 16. Every caller hands it a line as `T60_10` makes it, never one that `T53_00` has stepped, so the hex test is the first 16 bytes |
| `T51_30` | Copies a piece of 0FF00h bytes at a time, stepping both segments by 0FF0h, downwards from addresses made with offsets high enough to count down from | One loop, downwards from `Room + tail - 1` to `Room + end - 1`: the pieces were one byte after another in one direction all through |
| `T51_00` | Holds the segment of where the text would end against `EdSpace + ViewSeg` | `end >> 4 >= ed.EdSpace`, the room still in paragraphs, for N6 |
| `T01_10` | The last byte of the room: an offset of 0Fh in the last segment | `(place & 0x0F) == 0x0F && (place >> 4) + 1 >= ed.EdSpace` |
| `T16_00`, `T30_00`, `T32_00` | The line of a place in hex, the segment of its address less `ViewSeg` | `(u16)(place >> 4)`: the line in hex is 16 bits, N6's, and the cast says it. The 20 bits of `AddressOf` went where nothing cut: `ed.EdOffst = place & 0xFFFFFFF0UL` |
| `T80_02`, `T00_00` | Write and read the file 0FF00h bytes at a time, the segment stepped by 0FF0h | A pointer stepped by `PIECE` |
| `T72_00` | Takes `from` and `end` as offsets in a segment, and looks for the two characters in the two bytes before `end` wherever `end` is 2 or more | Takes `from`, `end` and `base`, where that segment began, and looks where `end - base >= 2`. This is the one thing that the original does by an address that shows: a last line of one byte that makes the two characters with the byte before it, as at the end of a text "...\r\n\r", is shown as no bytes, but where it is the first line of the window and stands at the start of a paragraph, where the character is shown. Ported as it is: `T00_20` hands the paragraph of `EdFirst`, which is the original's segment for that line, and for every line below it the test is true either way; `T73_10` hands the main data for the line buffer, which is the original's segment for that, so the two bytes in front of what the buffer holds are looked at for a line of one character too |
| `T00_20`, T00_42 | A line that does not end within 64K: the window gets what its segment has, to 0FFFFh, and the end is looked for a piece at a time | One call of `T72_00` with where the line ends. The window shows at most the columns before it and in it of a line, and the cursor is no further than 3,900 characters in, tabs among them: at most some 32K bytes, which both reach |
| `T32_00` | The viewer's search, `V82_00`, takes a segment and an offset and answers an offset | F4 has it take a text and an offset in it: `Room + base`, the paragraph of the place, and the place less `base`, as the assembly had them; `base + sought.end` is the place found |

**Held on this computer.** The old functions and the new, from
`T50_00` to `T54_00` with `T53_10`, were taken out of the two files by
a script, compiled by gcc for this computer with a few lines in place
of `vc.h` (an arena of 1.2 MB, `Room` in it at a segment of 3000h,
`AT` and `SEG_OF` as `vc.h` has them), and called alike on 400 texts:
short ones, and ones of 60K to 450K with lines of up to 200,000 bytes,
lines of 3,898 to 3,903 and of 65,500 to 65,540, ended by CR LF, LF CR,
CR, LF or nothing, with the two characters behind the end of the text.
`T53_00` at every place and line number, also from an address of
another segment than `AddressOf` makes; `T54_00` from the start of
every line; `T53_10` in hex; `T50_00` at the start of a line and at any
place; `T51_00` with a buffer shorter, as long and longer, the room
full and not. 854,385 checks, none that differs in what the two
answered, in the text, in the buffer or in the beeps. The script and
the program are `build/f5/`, not kept: about 150 lines. What it cannot
hold: the window, `T72_00` and `T00_20`, which the table reads.

**The steps added to a place**, of the brief, each read:

- `T71_00`, the screen's lines moved by one: the step of 16 bits, 160
  or FF60h, was added to the place of the main data, `MD_POINTER(
  MD_PLACE(to) + step)`. It is `(i32)(short)step / 2` cells added to the
  pointer, `stride`: FF60h is 80 cells back. The viewer's two calls and
  the editor's hand what they handed, and `T71_00` keeps its prototype.
- `T54_00`: `at`, an `i32`, from `place - 2` down, and `at - 2` read;
  it stops below 2, so nothing before the text is read.
- `T53_00`, `T53_10`, `T50_00`: `Room + end.at - 2`, with `end.at` at
  least two on from a place before the end, where it is read.
- `T51_00`: `Room + tail - 1` and `Room + end - 1`, with `tail` not
  below `EdEndBf`. Where the room is full and the line grows by more
  than the room has, `tail` wraps below 0 as a `u32`, as it did; the
  room is never under `MinView`, 8,000 bytes, so that is not
  reached.
- `T26_00`: `left`, an `i32`, the bytes from the cursor to `from` in the
  line buffer, where it was a difference of two places of the main
  data; not above 0 when the cursor is behind.
- `T00_20`: `Room + start - 2` behind `start < 2`.
- `T01_10`: `*(u16 *)&ed.EdOffst += 0x10`, the low word of the place
  stepped by a line of hex and back, without the carry, as the
  assembly does: a place within 16 bytes of a multiple of 64K draws
  the line 64K back. Left as it is, a bug of the original, and N6's to
  keep: it counts on the wrapping.
- `T72_00` in hex: the place shown is `(u32)(from - Room)`.

**The image.** `compare` of origin/main's build, saved before anything
was changed, with this one: "155 scenarios, 40 with nothing that
differs; 124 differences, 0 more in what was declared as changed, 137
in what may differ". The six of `copy` and `copy-dirs`, 84h before and

`setup-options-russia`, `stamps-russia`, and of those `DTA+42`, C3h

`edit.c`, so it is the program's file that differs there and not what

The tool knows such a byte since by one rule, `NAME_TAIL` of

**The records.** The words', of `edit.c`: `AddressOf` 24 and

**What N6 to N8 should know.**

- A place of the text is a `u32`, as `EdOffst`, `EdEndBf`, `EdLen` and
  `EdFirst` are: `struct Where`'s `place`, `struct Ending`'s `at`,
  `start` of `T00_20`, `base` of `T32_00`, the parameter of `T53_10`,
  `EndsAt` and `NoEnd`. They are the editor's places and go with those
  fields, which the cluster sorts; making them `i32` alone would have
  put a cast at every meeting. `struct Where` stays, a place and a line
  number, where the plan had it go: a line is a thing that the keys
  hand on, and N6's row names it.
- `T63_01(high, low)`, `T56_00`'s four halves, `HIGH` and `LOW` are as
  they were: the halves of a place, which a number of 32 bits does not
  need. `T63_01` is called with `HIGH(place), LOW(place)` everywhere.
- The four `i32` are new and signed by the rule: `length` of
  `T50_00`, `at` of `T54_00`, `left` of `T26_00`, `stride` of `T71_00`.
- The line in hex is `(u16)(place >> 4)` in three places, the 16 bits of
  `EdLine`; `end >> 4 >= ed.EdSpace` and `(place >> 4) + 1 >=
  ed.EdSpace` compare a number of 32 bits with the room in paragraphs,
  N6's to make bytes.
- `T72_00`'s `end - base >= 2` is the original's, and is to stay what
  it is when the numbers are sorted: it is a test of where an address
  is, not of the line.
- `*(u16 *)&ed.EdOffst` in `T01_10` counts on the wrap, above.
- `PIECE` is a count of 16 bits handed to `FileRead` and `FileWrite`
  with `count`, a `u16`.

### F8, the rest: done, and what a later piece should know

The words in the piece's fourteen files were fewer than the 165 that
the record's last line gave F8: that line counts `NEAR`, `MD_PLACE` and
`MD_POINTER` in every file, and most of them are in files that other
pieces have, `edit.c`, `copy.c`, `dirfunc.c`, `view.c`, `find.c`, and
the commands of a line. Of the fourteen, `help.c`, `keys.c`, `main.c`,
`menu.c`, `stcolor.c`, `sthelp.c`, `stopts.c` and `window.c` had any,
28 places on 25 lines; `commands.c`, `bars.c`, `system.c`, `setup.c`
and `stmain.c` had none, and `start.c` has only what F9 is to change.
With the callers of the routines that changed, the piece was one
commit, and was not cut.

**What changed.**

- `SavWin` and `ResWin` of `window.c` take the buffer as a pointer,
  `u16 *` and `const u16 *`, where they took its place in the main

  of `dialog.c` makes of the offset that the box's table names
  (`MD_AT`, which stays), `(u16 *)((u8 *)&md + head->saved)`, as the
  file makes a field of `data`. Every caller that handed
  `MD_PLACE(md.WinBuf)`, of `md.ErrBuf` or of `md.ErrBuf1` hands the
  array: 30 lines in 11 files, 18 of them in other pieces' files, one
  line each, `cmdline.c` 4, `treebox.c` 3, `find.c` 3, `drive.c` 2,
  `usermenu.c` 2, `edit.c` 2, `view.c` 1. Those that hand `box.saved`
  or `where.saved` are as they were.
- `InSt10` of `dialog.c` takes the text as a `const u8 *`: its four
  callers lost their `MD_PLACE`, two in `dialog.c` and one each in
  `cmdline.c`, `treebox.c` and `copy.c`.
- The registers of the main loop. `r->si` and `r->di` were set to
  `MD_PLACE` of `md.MenuBuf` and of `IniSave` at `Func06`, of
  `md.CrnPath` and `md.DosPth` at `Func07`, and `r->si` to `md.WinBuf`
  behind the speed search: what the assembly has in SI and DI there.
  Nothing reads them as those leave them: the three commands that take
  SI and DI are the mouse's, which only `Func21` asks for, and it sets

- `help.c`: `(u16)(MD_PLACE(NEAR(text)) - MD_PLACE(hd.HlpInfo))`, how

  difference of two pointers, cut to 16 bits as the original's

- `stopts.c`: three `NEAR` of what `FndLet` and `TxtNum` answer, which

**What stays, and why.**

- `keys.c`, `MD_PLACE` twice on one line: the leak of `F00_50` into BX
