### P, the panel without its limit: done, and what a later piece should know

**What the user decided.** On 14 October 2026, as `CLAUDE.md` has it:
a panel's memory grows as its directory needs, with no ceiling of
entries and nothing reserved for it beforehand, and a scenario of it is
kept only if it runs in reasonable time, the one that took ten minutes
being dropped. A first form of the piece had taken a block of some
1.5 MB for each panel when the program started, as much as 65,536
entries take, or a quarter of the memory where there was less; that
was a ceiling and a reservation both, and is not what landed.

**What there is.** A panel holds as many entries of a directory as there
is memory for, where the original stops at 2,703 (`DEVIATIONS.md`, 27).
A panel's block begins with `struct Places` of `vc.h`, 32 bytes: the
block's length, `Bytes`, three words unused, and the four places of the
list, `CurAdr`, `First`, `EndBuf` and `EndFul`, `i32` each, in the
paragraph right in front of the panel, `PLACES(panel)`. The panel keeps
the original's words as `CurAdr16`, `First16`, `EndBuf16` and
`EndFul16`, unset and unread, so that its layout, `WCBini` and the setup
file are as they were, and a read of the old name does not compile.
`ENTRY` has no cut. `DSKBUF` is an `i32`.

- `Init11` of `start.c` takes each panel's block as `PANEL_LEAST`, the
  original's 64K and the places, which holds 2,703 entries, and the
  room behind them as before, the largest block that there is.
- `ReDr00` of `read.c` ends the list a paragraph and two entries,
  `PANEL_TAIL`, short of the block's end, as the original does short of
  64K. Where DOS has another entry to give there, it asks `PanelGrow`
  of `start.c` for a longer block and goes on; only where that answers
  0 does it beep and stop, as the original does at 2,703.
- `PanelGrow` makes the room as short as the old list that it holds, but
  not shorter than `LEAST_ROOM`, and the panel's block twice as long, or
  as long as the largest block that there is if it is longer than the
  panel's and twice is too much. The extender moves a block that cannot
  grow where it is, with what it holds (`TODO.md`, "X", rows 8 and 9):
  the panel goes behind what is taken, and the room, made shorter,
  stays where it begins. Both answers are taken as addresses whatever
  they are, since DPMI promises neither.
- When the directory has been read, `PanelFit` makes the block as short
  as the list with its tail, but not shorter than `PANEL_LEAST`; and
  `ReDir`, behind `ReDr50`, which still reads the old list in the room,
  takes the room again, `RoomAgain`: given back and taken as the largest
  block that there is, where it may begin elsewhere. That is done only
  where a block was made longer or shorter, which no scenario does.
- A block that moves has the four pointers to the panels, `LeftPanel`,
  `RightPanel`, `CurrentPanel` and `OtherPanel`, made to point where it
  is (`Moved` of `start.c`). `ReDir` takes the panel as `struct WCBdef
  **` and leaves it there; its one caller, `Init50` of `main.c`, takes
  `panel` and `wcb` again from it, and the main loop takes the current
  panel from `CurrentPanel` behind `Init50`, as it did. Nothing else
  holds a pointer to a panel or into a list across `ReDir`: a place in
  a list is an offset from the panel everywhere, the main data's words
  of it too.
- The numbers of entries that go round the main loop for the mouse are
  `i32`: SI and DI of `struct Regs`, which carry nothing else, and
  `last`, the number that the original has in DX for `F01_05`. DX keeps
  it as well, cut to its 16 bits with `wraps`, for what reads DX as the
  loop leaves it; AX the number under the mouse, as the original has
  it, for the double click. `Func40` of `main.c` takes a number below
  the first entry for one above the last, which is what the wrapping of
  16 bits made of it.
- `NumbF` of an entry, the order in which DOS gave it, stays the
  original's word of 16 bits: an entry's layout is the original's, 24
  bytes, which every place that steps through a list counts in and which
  the image's tool reads by the original's listing, and a directory of
  DOS has 65,536 entries at the most. `number` in `ReDr00` is an `i32`,
  and the cut is written with that reason. A panel stops at 65,536
  entries for good, as the user decided later on 14 October 2026
  (`CLAUDE.md`): a system that is not DOS shows at most so many entries
  of a directory, which is declared when such a system comes.

Every number that held a place in a panel is an `i32`, by the record of
`harness/width.py`: `struct Shown`, `struct OldList`, `FnFile`, `NearFl`,
`NumAdr`, `ChgAdr`, `F00_50`, `Search`, and the variables of `cmdline.c`,
`commands.c`, `copy.c`, `dirfunc.c`, `enter.c`, `files.c`, `keys.c`,
`panel.c`, `place.c`, `read.c` and `usermenu.c`. What stays 16 bits:
BX and DX that `F00_50` leaves for Rename, cut with a comment that no
such cut is 0; the tree's offsets, `TREE_OFFSET`, its list being short.
The counts that fitted by 2,703, in `info.c`, `main.c` and `panel.c`,
are shown in their 32 bits, or say why they fit. `FncSel` of
`dirfunc.c` tested a file above the page by a difference wrapping in 16
bits; it tests `address >= First` now.

**The harness.** `harness/dataimage.py` knows a build with the places by
the symbol `PanelGrow_` and puts them, cut to 16 bits, into the panel's
original words when it reads the image, so that such a build is held
against one from before word for word; the 32 bytes in front of the
panel are a part that a build from before has not. `KEPT` of
`harness/le.py` is `PANEL_LEAST` twice, 32 bytes more than a panel was,
for where a second copy of the program is loaded; a scenario that ran a
program with a panel that has grown would have it elsewhere, and there
is none. `harness/int16.txt` has the places of the kind `widen` with
their reason, `harness/width.txt` the fields unused.

**The test of merges.** `harness/conflicts.py`, asked by the test
`portable_c-words`, fails for a line of a merge's conflict in any file
that git tracks but for `src/asm` and the goldens.

**The scenario that was dropped.** `panel-full` made C:\WORK\FULL of
2,873 empty files by copies to masks, thirteen letters in each of the
first three places of the name and then the 676 of the last four
letters to the extension Z, every copy of files that both programs
list, and was held to the original's golden by a patch of the rows that
differ: the last files of the list, the count of what is selected, the
count of the files in the Info panel. It took the original six minutes
and the portable C eight to ten, and was dropped as the user decided:
the time is DOS's, creating some 2,900 files in a directory that grows,
and a directory has to have 2,704 entries to pass the original's
limit. Its steps, for whoever wants to see it again: `F7 "full" Enter`,
`Enter`, `Shift+F5` with `"c:\work\empty.dat" Tab
"c:\work\full\aaaaaaaa.aaa" Enter`; then for each of the first three
places of the name `GrayPlus "*.*" Enter` and, for each letter from b to
m, `Ctrl+m F5` with the mask that has the letter in that place, `"b*.*"`,
`"?b*.*"`, `"??b*.*"`, `Enter`; then `GrayPlus` of `"j*.*"` to `"m*.*"`
and `F5 "*.z" Enter`; then `Home`, `End`, `GrayPlus "*.*" Enter` and
`Ctrl+l`. In a copy of the harness, with the scenario put back, its
golden derived from the original (`python3 harness/goldens.py derive
panel-full`, six minutes), its patch made (`python3 harness/goldens.py
patch --tree portable_c panel-full`), and the step's time raised
(`STEP_TIME` of `harness/scenarios.py`, 1,200 seconds: the last copy
takes longer than 300 on a host that is busy).

**How growing was seen.** On a build of the tree with `PANEL_LEAST`
made `sizeof(struct Places) + 0x1C00` in a copy, a block that holds 273
entries (the panel's fields, 0x262 bytes, have to fit too), configured
and built in `build/` as a copy of `main` is: the scenarios
`enter-many` and `enter-many-selected`, whose directory of 288 files
the panel then does not hold, passed as they pass with the build of the
tree, against the original's golden and the patch of the second, and
their images had the left panel's block grown, moved behind the right
one's and made as short as its list again, 7,648 bytes where it began
with 7,216, with the room taken again behind it and the pointers to the
panels where the block is (`python3 harness/dataimage.py show`). Both
scenarios run a command afterwards, so the room was given back and
taken again with the panel where it had gone. That is a part of the
program replaced in a test build, as "Scenarios" of `CLAUDE.md` allows,
and is not kept. With the tree as it is, `panel-full` was run in a copy
of the harness as above, twice, on a host with a load of some 34 on
four processors, and was given up in its last copy both times, at 300
and at 1,200 seconds, with the program still copying, 63 and 96 files
from the end, before the read that grows the panel: the time is DOS's,

- The stub and the program for Linux are held by the same test: a file
  `_posix.c` wants `harness/stubcheck.py` to read it too, from the
  `compiled.txt` of that build.
- A function that another file calls is declared in `vc.h`, not in the
  file that calls it: clang-tidy names a function that no header
  declares and that is not static.
- clang-tidy of another version fails the test: judge its new checks,
  then change `VERSION` there and the comment at the top of
  `.clang-tidy`.

### MD, the main data read as bytes: done

clang-tidy 23 with `clang-analyzer-security.ArrayBound` and
`clang-analyzer-security.PointerSub` alone, over the common code with
the stub's command, named 23 places (13 and 10). 21 are the program
reading its main data across fields, and read now as what they are:

  `MD_AT(field)` of `tables.h` moved there, the place of a field as a
  number (`MD_AT(DTA.FilAttr)` takes a field of a field). A read across
  fields is `MD_BYTES + MD_AT(field) + n`, or `MD_BYTES[...]`.
- ArrayBound: `TRELIST` (the tree's list begins in its header's last
  field: `main.c`, `treebox.c`, `tree.c` twice); `LIST` of `menu.c`
  (an item of 80h or more in front of `TmpBuf`, twice); the byte in

  one block, and in `sthelp.c` the buffer at `offsetof` likewise:

- PointerSub: `MD_PLACE` of a field is the field's place, `MD_AT`:

  name's place in `dirfunc.c`, `EPB_WAS` of `exec.c` (3 named, 1

| | `F80_00` | 6 | `F80_05`, the name typed if there is room, a helper, for the file under the cursor and in the loop over the selected ones |
| | `F68_25` | 2 | `break` |
| `dirfunc.c` | `F38_40` | 16 | the box opened and closed round `DeleteFile` and `RemoveDir`, which return where the jumps went, `WALK` for a directory whose files go first; `F38_43` and `F38_54` helpers; F38_57, two lines, written twice where the command stops with no box open |
| | `F38_70` | 6 | the box round `F38_72` |
| | `M30_50` | 7 | the box round `M30_51`, with `M30_56` |
| | `M30_60` | 17 | `return M30_75()` |
| | `F47_01` | 1 | `F47_03` |
| | `F48_00` | 2 | a flag that the mask names every file |
| | `M30_00` | 1 | the two lines of M30_07 written twice |

Stay: `Loop` of `main.c`, 4, the main loop, a state machine that
mirrors the assembly on purpose; and `FncSel` of `dirfunc.c`, 2, whose
loop over the selected files is entered in the middle, at `one`, for
the file under the cursor, and goes on from there when nothing is
selected and the command is not for one file: a loop with two ways in.

Read and judged otherwise than the assessment: `F68_00`, which it named
among the hard ones, has loops with one way in each once Up and Down
fall into End and Home as the second line of their cases and the
search for a letter leaves its loop with the row or without it;
`F77_00`, whose loop was entered at F77_02 with the first key, is that
loop with the reading of a key at its end; `F80_00`'s file under the
cursor went into the loop and out of it at once, so what both do is a
helper and the loop has one way in; `Init50` is the same with three
lines. A loop that is entered in the middle and goes round from there,
as `FncSel`'s, kept its jumps.

Seventeen static helpers, each named for its label in the assembly
where it is the code there, `DeleteFile` and `RemoveDir` for what they
do, each said at its head. Four flags and one number, `READ_` of
`read.c`, say which way a jump went: an `enum` held in an `i32`, since
`int16.py` takes a variable of an `enum` type for a number of either
width. `key` of `F68_00` has a value from the start, as 5b gave three:
clang's `-Wconditional-uninitialized` cannot tell that it is read only
where `Input` has set it. A label's name stands in a comment where the
label was; where the C's label had a name of its own, `same`, `end`,
`older`, `shown`, `wake`, the assembly's stands in its place.

What no scenario runs, by the original's instructions that
`harness/ported.py` lists as out of reach, each read once more side
by side with the old code: in `F20_02` a current directory that DOS
has not told, PathEr, and the other panel's directory that DOS will
not go to, the `else` that marks the drive unknown; in
`M30_56` the box for attributes that DOS refuses for another reason
than a drive that is not ready; in `FtErr1` an error of the FAT, the
flag `fatal`; in `Init50` the drive chosen where none was noted, and
in `ErrRdy` the middle button, lines that did not change. Every other
instruction of the original's routines ran. That an instruction ran
says nothing of which way a jump went: the jumps to a shared end,
ReDr26, F38_43, M30_56, M30_75, F47_03 and F38_57, were each read
against the old code.

The harness: `DelEr_B` and `CntDi_B` are handed to `F38_43`, which no
form of `harness/reads.py` knows, and have entries of `REVIEWED`
there. `harness/width.txt` has the helpers' numbers, with the reasons
of the numbers they came from, carried by a script (the record keyed
by its first line, the place of a sign by its line, from the committed

`F80_00` (the last in `harness/int16.txt`) keep their reasons. The
records of `hostcheck.py` and `words.py` did not move.

**What judged it.** The whole suite, fourteen tests, 158 scenarios, no
golden and no patch changed (the whole suite, `reads.py` being shared;
a piece that touches only the portable C and its records runs `-R
portable_c`). The code is 536 bytes longer than `main`'s at aedea88,
on which the images were held before the rebase, so against `main`'s build
every scenario differs in all of the room. Against `main`'s build
padded to the same length of code, a function of 133 byte stores to a

1D186h in both, every segment of the map where this build has it):
150 of 158 scenarios with nothing that differs, `blank-timed` and

N22, G3 and G2 met, `comspec`, `ended`, `second-copy`, `start-screen`,
`start-setup`, whose second copy of the program lives in the room with

## The compiler's lost cut: what Open Watcom does, and where

`wcc386 -os` makes `movsx eax,al` of `(u16)(signed char)c` that goes on
into 32 bits, where C says FFFEh and not FFFFFFFEh ("The compiler, at
such a call", above; `harness/cut.py` is the test that was being
written against it as this was, and is spoken of below as it was read
then). This is what that fault
is, where it is in the compiler's source, and what follows for a tree
that is about to say every narrowing and every change of sign by a
cast. Nothing of the program or of the harness was changed for it.

What was run and what was read are kept apart below. Run: the pinned
compiler, "Open Watcom C x86 32-bit Optimizing Compiler, Version 2.0
beta Oct 1 2026 06:32:26 (64-bit)", and `wcc` of the same download for
16 bits. Read: the compiler's source at the commit of the release,
`e28568669775a7119f381f3b37d21745d8afcfb6`, which is what the tag
`2026-10-01-Build` of github.com/open-watcom/open-watcom-v2 names, the
tag in the URL that `CMakeLists.txt` pins. The source was fetched for
the reading alone and is gone again; the compiler was not built, so
that the lines below are the cause is a conclusion, by what they
predict.

**The cause.** `DoConversionOps` of `bld/cg/c/peepopt.c`, the code
generator's peephole optimiser, lines 577 to 597 at that commit:

    if( ins->head.opcode == OP_CONVERT && next->head.opcode == OP_CONVERT ) {
        if( ins->result == next->operands[0] &&
            ins->type_class == next->base_type_class ) {
            /*
             * change (cnv i1 -> i2; cnv i2 -> i4) into
             *        (cnv i1 -> i2; cnv i1 -> i4) and let dead code take care of
             * the first ins if it is not needed
             ...
             * watch for converting down - bad to fold
             */
            if( ins->type_class < ins->base_type_class )
                return( false );
            next->base_type_class = ins->base_type_class;
            next->operands[0] = ins->operands[0];

Of two conversions in one block, A to B and then B to C, it makes the
second a conversion of the first one's operand, A to C, and so takes
whether C is filled with the sign or with zeros from A alone. That is
right as the comment has it, for two types with a sign, and wrong
where B has no sign and A has one. The one thing it watches for is
"converting down", by the order of the type classes (`U1`, `I1`,
`U2`, `I2`, `U4`, `I4`, `U8`, `I8`, two classes of pointers, `FS`,
`FD`, `FL`, in `bld/cg/h/typcldef.h`), and pointers, which are far
ones only: a near pointer is `U2` or `U4`. So the fold is made
whenever B is not below A in that order, and it is wrong exactly when
A has a sign, B is wider and has none, and C is wider than B or is a
floating type.

What else those lines say. The first two of these, and the floating
types and the new value for the source further down, were said from
the lines before they were run; the rest explains what was known:

- The two conversions have to be in one block, with nothing between
  that may redefine the first one's result or its operand
  (`_IsReDefinedBy`, tested for each instruction between). A jump
  between them, a call when the variable's address has been handed
  out, a store through a pointer that may be the variable, and a new
  value for the source all keep the fold away.
- An instruction that names something `volatile` is not looked at
  (`VolatileIns`, in `PeepOptBlock`).
- `ins->type_class == next->base_type_class`: the second conversion
  has to start from the very class that the first ended in. A
  conversion between two types of one size is no instruction at all
  (`NeedConvert` of `bld/cg/c/bldins.c`: the lengths are the same, so
  the value is only given the other type). `(u16)(short)(signed
  char)c` is therefore a conversion `I1` to `I2` and one `U2` to `U4`,
  the classes differ, and nothing is folded: a `short` between is
  right by how the fold is written, not by the order of the passes.
- `(u16)(int)x`, `(u16)(u32)x` and their like are the same as
  `(u16)x`: `DemoteTree` of `bld/cg/c/treeconv.c` gives the inner
  conversion the narrower type when the tree is built. Arithmetic
  that the front end folds to nothing is no instruction either.
  Arithmetic that stays is an instruction between the two
  conversions with a result of its own, so the second conversion does
  not start from the first one's result.
- The calls of the peephole optimiser lie under
  `_IsntModel( CGSW_GEN_NO_OPTIMIZATION )`: two in `PostOptimize` of
  `bld/cg/c/generate.c`, and one in `CommonSex` of `bld/cg/c/cse.c`,
  which `generate.c` calls under the same test; a fourth, in
  `PropIndexes` of the loop optimiser, was not followed that far.
  That is `-od`, and no other option of the compiler: the peephole
  is not one of the optimisations that `-o` chooses among. It is behind both front
  ends and in the code generator of every target, 16 bits included.

**The table.** Every chain of two conversions among the eight integer
types of 8 to 64 bits, 392 chains, each as twelve functions, compiled
with the build's options for a file of the tree (`-3r -mf -s -zl -zls
-os`), linked for Linux with the C library of the same download, run
on this computer on sixteen values and held against gcc. Eight chains
are wrong, the eight that the rule above names, and no other:

| from | to | and on to |
|---|---|---|
| s8 | u16 | s32, u32, s64, u64 |
| s8 | u32 | s64, u64 |
| s16 | u32 | s64, u64 |

and each of the eight in the same forms:

| form | | |
|---|---|---|
| `(C)(B)x` in one expression | wrong | `movsx eax,al` |
| `B v = (B)x; return (C)v;` | wrong | |
| the same with no cast written | wrong | |
| through a global, `g = (B)x; return (C)g;` | wrong | stored rightly, read wrongly |
| through a variable whose address is kept, nothing between | wrong | |
| the source read through a pointer, or returned by a function | wrong | |
| `B v = (B)x; if (flag) count++; return (C)v;` | right | two blocks |
| `B v = (B)x; look(&v); return (C)v;` | right | the call may write `v` |
| `volatile B v = (B)x; return (C)v;` | right | |
| across a return, `(C)mid(x)` with `B mid(A)` | right | wrong with `-ox` or `-oe`, which expand `mid` in place |
| as an argument, `take((B)x)` with `C take(B)` | right | `take` cuts for itself; wrong with `-ox`, `-oe` |

The other 384 chains are right in all twelve forms: every narrowing,
every change of sign at one size, a widening from a type without a
sign, and a widening with a sign both times. With `-ot`, `-ox`, no
`-o` at all, and `-os -oe` it is the same eight; with `-od` none.
The compiler for 16 bits does the same, read in its listing and not
run: `cbw; cwd` for s8 to u16 to a long of either sign, wrong and
right in the same forms, of which ten of the twelve were read. The
compiler for C++ makes `movsx eax,al` of the first form too.

Beyond the eight, by the same lines, each tried:

- A floating type as the third: `(double)(u16)c` for a signed char is
  `cbw` and `fild word ptr`, -2 where C says 65534, and so are s8 or
  s16 by way of u32, and s32 by way of u64. Six chains tried, six
  wrong, right with `-od`.
- A pointer as the third, in 32 bits: `(void *)(u16)c`, `base[(u16)c]`
  and `base + (u16)c` are `movsx`.
- The source may be anything of a signed type of that size: a
  bit-field declared `signed char`, worked out by two shifts in a
  byte, goes wrong like a variable.
- A step that the compiler folds to nothing does not help: `(u16)(c +
  0)`, `- 0`, `| 0`, `^ 0`, `* 1`, `/ 1`, `<< 0`, `>> 0`, `& -1`,
  `-(-c)`, and `(u16)(c + 1 - 1)`, are all `movsx eax,al`. Written
  out nobody writes them; a macro that is 0 does.
- A step that stays does: `(u16)(c - 1)`, `(u16)~~c`, `(u16)(c + k)`
  for a variable `k` that is 0, and the mask `& 0xFFFF` on either
  side of the cast, are right. Those rest on the instruction still
  being there when the peephole last runs, which nothing promises of
  the mask.
- A new value for the source between the two, `u16 v = (u16)x; x =
  ...; return v;`, is right, and a store through a pointer to a u16
  between is right: the two tests of `_IsReDefinedBy`.
- An integer that a floating type rounds, `(double)(float)i` and
  `(int)(float)i` for 16,777,217, keeps all its digits with `-os`
  where a variable is between, and is rounded with `-od`. The lines
  say so too: `FS` is above every integer, so the fold is made. But
  in one expression it is not rounded with `-od` either, so the
  coprocessor's own precision is in it, and this was not taken
  further.

**Upstream.** `peepopt.c` is the same file on the project's default
branch on 13 October 2026, commit
`1f178ef1b1a1bb06492759f8e2b76c2a7f39e9b6`. The lines are in the
first commit of the repository, of 2002, with the same tests in the
same order: the fault is as old as the published source, and every
release since has it by that. A dozen searches of the project's issues
(sign extension, `movsx`, `movzx`, `cdq`, conversion, cast, signed
char, unsigned short, wrong code, `peepopt`, `DoConversionOps`) and
one of the web found no report of it. The nearest, issue 822, is of
the type of the constant -32768 and another matter.

**The mend**, described and not tried, since the compiler is not
built here: in `DoConversionOps`, behind the test for "converting
down", leave the pair alone when the first conversion is from a class
with a sign (`_IsSigned`, of `split.h`) to an integer class without
one and the second goes on to a wider class (`TypeClassSize`) or to a
floating one. A dozen lines and an `#include`. The rounding by a
floating type, above, is no part of it or of the report: it was seen
and not understood. The plainest form of the mend, never to fold
behind a conversion from a signed class to one without a sign, loses
only folds like s8 to u32 to u16.

**What it means for the tree.** With no number of 64 bits and no
floating type, a program of 32 bits meets the fault in one shape, a
signed type of 8 bits made a type of 16 bits without a sign that goes
on into 32, which is what `harness/cut.py` says. And the casts that
the tree is about to lean on are honoured as far as this fold goes: a
narrowing first conversion is never folded, a change of sign at one
size is no conversion, and a fold whose second conversion narrows is
right; the 384 chains are the evidence. What the finder of
`harness/cut.py` should have besides, as it was read while it was
being written:

- It looks through casts, a `+` in front, a comma and a choice. By
  the lines it would have to look through every step that the
  compiler folds to nothing, of which the list above is what was
  tried. Simpler and closed: take arithmetic for a step that changes
  the number only where an operand of it is no constant, and take
  nothing but a `short` between for the form of the tree.
- A floating type is to be refused as a number of 64 bits is: with
  one, a `short` made a u32 is wrong as well.
- `-oe`, or `-ox`, which has it, expands a function in place and
  brings two conversions into one block that a call kept apart. The
  check that holds `harness/cutcheck.c` to its instructions compiles
  with the build's options, so a build that got such an option would
  show there.

**A report for the compiler's project**, to file as it is; nothing
was sent.

> **cg: peephole fold of two conversions extends the sign through an
> unsigned type: `(unsigned long)(unsigned short)c` of a `signed char`
> is `movsx eax,al`**
>
> Open Watcom C x86 32-bit Optimizing Compiler, Version 2.0 beta Oct
> 1 2026 06:32:26 (64-bit), the snapshot 2026-10-01-Build, commit
> e28568669775a7119f381f3b37d21745d8afcfb6. The same in `wpp386` and
> in `wcc` (16 bits) of that build. The code is unchanged on master
> and has been there since the first commit.
>
>     #include <stdio.h>
>
>     unsigned long lost( signed char c )
>     {
>         return( (unsigned short)c );
>     }
>
>     unsigned long kept( signed char c )
>     {
>         return( (unsigned short)(short)c );
>     }
>
>     double lost_fp( signed char c )
>     {
>         return( (unsigned short)c );
>     }
>
>     int main( void )
>     {
>         printf( "%lx %lx %g\n", lost( -2 ), kept( -2 ), lost_fp( -2 ) );
>         return( 0 );
>     }
>
> `wcc386 -bt=linux lost.c`, linked with `system linux`, and likewise
> with `-os`, `-ot`, `-ox`. Expected, and printed with `-od`:
> `fffe fffe 65534`. Printed: `fffffffe fffe -2`.
>
> `lost` is `movsx eax,al; ret`, where the conversion to `unsigned
> short` gives 0xFFFE and the one to `unsigned long` has to fill with
> zeros (`cbw; movzx eax,ax`, which is what `kept` gets). `lost_fp` is
> `cbw; mov [esp],eax; fild word ptr [esp]`. With `wcc`, `lost` is
> `cbw; cwd`. In general: a conversion from a signed integer type to a
> wider unsigned one, followed in the same block by a conversion to a
> still wider integer type, of either sign, or to a floating type; the
> second is made with the sign of the first one's operand. Of the 392
> chains of two conversions among the integer types of 8 to 64 bits,
> exactly eight are wrong: s8 to u16 to s32, u32, s64 or u64; s8 to
> u32 to s64 or u64; s16 to u32 to s64 or u64. It also happens through
> a variable, a global or a field, when both conversions end up in one
> block.
>
> Cause: `DoConversionOps` in `bld/cg/c/peepopt.c` changes `cnv A ->
> B; cnv B -> C` into `cnv A -> B; cnv A -> C`, and refuses only
> pointers and "converting down" (`ins->type_class <
> ins->base_type_class`). `cnv I1 -> U2; cnv U2 -> U4` becomes `cnv I1
> -> U4`, which extends the sign.
>
> Proposed mend, behind the test for converting down (it needs
> `split.h` for `_IsSigned`); not built or tested:
>
>     if( _IsSigned( ins->base_type_class )
>       && !_IsSigned( ins->type_class )
>       && !_IsFloating( ins->type_class )
>       && ( _IsFloating( next->type_class )
>         || TypeClassSize[next->type_class] > TypeClassSize[ins->type_class] ) )
>         return( false );

## An implementation of `sys.h` for tests: future work

The road of the portable C (`CLAUDE.md`, "The portable C") has DOS as
the layer at its step 3, `sys.h` as it is, the implementation for DOS
behind it at step 4, and at step 5 a second implementation that builds
and is not meant to run, a stub. An implementation of `sys.h` made for
tests would be another: one that does run, on this
computer, built by clang, with the common code of the program above it,
and that answers the program where a system would. It is future work,
on the user's word of 13 October 2026, with everything that it would
give written down here. It is not started, and is not to be started
without the user. The stub of step 5 stays a stub: making the
implementation for tests in its place was proposed, and not taken.

What is here was found on that day by reading the tree as it was at
7fc7a51 and by counting, with nothing of the program run. Of every
figure it is said whether it was counted, and by what, or is an
estimate:

- "IR" is counted in what clang wrote. clang 23 was given every file of
  `src/portable_c/` for 32 bits, `clang -m32 -ffreestanding -std=gnu99
  -O0 -S -emit-llvm`, with `__interrupt`, `__loadds` and
  `__declspec(x)` defined away, and `dialog.c` and the files of tables
  in a copy with the `LAID_OUT` lines taken out. It took 54 of the 55
  files, all but `resident.c` with its `_asm`, and nothing counted so
  is of that file. In what it wrote a script counted the functions, of
  each its instructions, which is what a share of the program is a
  share of below, its conditional branches, `br i1`, the cases of its
  `switch` statements, and the functions that it calls by name; two
  calls go through a pointer and were not followed. That clang reads a
  file says nothing of whether it would run: a panel is a segment's
  number there still.
- "Regex" is a pattern counted in the source without its comments, or
  in the listing of the original.
- "Read" is sorted by reading, one thing at a time.
- "The test's" is what the scenarios' test printed when it last ran
  before that day.

### What it would give

1. **The sanitizers under the steps of the scenarios that there are.**
   clang's address sanitizer stops a program at a read or a write
   outside the object that a pointer is of, on every path that a step
   takes and whatever the form of the read. The project has had to find
   such reads by other means: `harness/reads.py` knows a read behind
   the end of a constant by its form, or by an entry of `REVIEWED`
   made by reading, and `CLAUDE.md` tells what it was made for, five
   constants with a zero byte too many, `CrLf_S` among them, and
   `User_S`, copied as 80 bytes from another file and found last. In a
   flat memory, step 2 of the road, what lies behind an object is no
   longer what the original has there, so the sanitizer's list is the
   list of the places where the program goes by the layout of the
   memory. The sanitizer of undefined behaviour stops at a shift by
   too much, at a sum with a sign that does not fit, and at a number
   read or written at an address that is not even, which
   `harness/hostcheck.py` says at its top that it cannot see. For
   arithmetic it has two groups besides, which are no undefined
   behaviour and are switched on by name: `-fsanitize=integer`, which
   stops where a number without a sign wraps round, and
   `-fsanitize=implicit-conversion`, which stops where a number loses
   bits or changes its sign as it is put into a narrower type. Under
   the steps of the scenarios those say every place where a number
   does wrap or is cut, which is the reading list for step 2 of the
   road, what is to stay 16 bits and what is to be widened: a place
   that the program counts on stops like one that is a fault, so it
   is a list to read and not a test. What none of them finds is
   wrapping that is missing: a number that wrapped round at 16 bits
   on DOS and, in an int of 32, no longer does. Nothing overflows
   there, the result is another, and only a comparison says so: the
   scenarios, and 8 below. The memory sanitizer stops at a value that
   is used and was
   never set: `SetStat` and the entry handed DOS a `name` that nothing
   had set, DS and DX as the stack had them (`CLAUDE.md`, "Moving a
   file to the system's functions"), and the audit with clang's
   warnings named two variables, both set. The first two sanitizers
   are there for a program of 32 bits and the third for one of 64 only:
   that is what is known of clang, and was not tried.
2. **The suite in seconds, on every build and in a CI.** An estimate:
   nothing was run. What it rests on was measured, in "Ways of testing
   that were tried": 77% of a scenario's time is the machine running
   while the harness waits, most of it the program waiting for the
   timer while a box grows. A clock that the implementation moves on
   when the program says that it is idle takes that time away, and no
   machine is started. The two tests of the scenarios take a little
   under two minutes each today.
3. **Mutation testing that can be paid for, which measures what
   coverage does not.** That a branch ran does not mean that a screen
   shows what it is for. `harness/notice.py` asks that of one change at
   a time, with a build of a copy of the tree and a run of the
   scenarios for each, minutes; it found three branches that no
   scenario noticed in one batch of nine routines ("What batches have
   lost time to"), and the table of the blanker's stars was three bytes
   wrong with every scenario passing. One change to each conditional
   branch of the program is some 3,300 runs: at seconds a run that is
   an afternoon, an estimate, and at minutes it is not done. What
   comes of it is the list of the branches that the goldens do not
   watch.
4. **The first measurement of the C's own branches.** What is measured
   today is the instructions of the original that ran, 22,603 of the
   22,981 that the 50 batches translate, 98.4% (the test's), and of the
   C only that each function of a batch was entered
   (`check_translation` of `harness/ported.py`). What is not measured,
   of the original or of the C, is which way a jump went, and it cannot
   be had from what is recorded: QEMU logs a block once, when it
   translates it. The C has 3,297 conditional branches and 420 cases of
   `switch` statements in its 521 functions outside `dos.c`, and
   `dos.c` has 5 conditional branches in its 102 (IR); the listing of
   the original has some 3,000 conditional jumps and loops (regex,
   3,008, and a line that the pattern does not take is not counted).
   The source has 2,406 `if`, 153 `while`, 439 `for`, and 215 `&&` and
   132 `||` (regex, the files of code). clang's coverage by the source
   says of every branch how often it went each way, `llvm-cov show
   --show-branches=count`. Nobody knows the figure today, and none was
   guessed. MC/DC is not worth its cost: the conditions came from
   single conditional jumps, and few are of more than one part. What
   to report is three lists that are never added up: the branches that
   a scenario of the bench runs, where the original is the judge; those
   that only a test on this computer runs, where reading is; and those
   listed with a reason, as `unreached` is today. Only the first is
   fidelity.
5. **The paths that the bench cannot produce.** `harness/ported.py`
   lists 378 instructions of the original as out of reach, with 94
   reasons (counted there; the batches of the setup program had none
   yet). Sorted by the kind of the reason (read):

   | Why no scenario gets there | Instructions | With an implementation for tests |
   |---|---|---|
   | DOS refuses a call that it grants on the bench: a file that it will not delete, attributes that it will not set, a directory that it will not go to | 79 | reached: the test says the answer |
   | Another machine: a CGA with snow, a network, a CD-ROM, no mouse, DESQview or TopView, no EGA | 60 | reached: the test says the answer |
   | A disk that is full, a write that comes up short, the next disk | 43 | reached: the test says the answer |
   | Memory that runs out, or more than there is room for | 42 | reached in part: where the program asks for memory and is refused |
   | Another version of DOS | 30 | reached: the test says the answer |
   | A drive that is not ready, the critical error | 19 | reached: the critical error is a call back that the program hands over since S2 |
   | The time of day at the end of a minute, an hour, a day | 14 | reached: the clock is the implementation's |
   | A country that neither bench has | 11 | reached, also by calling the routine with the country's record |
   | Code that nothing calls, or input that no step makes: markup that no text has, a file with a line end in every two bytes, a path of 68 characters | 80 | some 50 by calling the routine itself or with a file made for it (an estimate); the rest nothing reaches |

   So 298 of the 378 are of the kinds that such an implementation

### What it has to be

The rule of "Scenarios" in `CLAUDE.md` is that a test puts no stand-in
where something is that the project does not own, and that what a test
knows of DOS, the BIOS and the machine it gets from the real ones.
`sys.h` is the project's. What a function of it promises is a statement
about a system all the same: that `FileWrite` answers with fewer bytes
on a disk that is full is so of DOS, whoever wrote the header. So an
implementation for tests is within the rule only as this:

- It knows nothing of its own of what a system does.
- It answers what a test tells it to, the test's premise in so many
  words, "the third write answers 5 of 512": scripted. It has a queue
  of answers and no more.
- Or it answers what the real system was recorded answering on the
  bench, call for call: replay. Such a record is derived, as a golden
  is, and never edited, and is taken only from a run whose screens were
  the original's golden's.
- Where a premise of a scripted test can be made to happen on the
  bench, a small program asks the real DOS and holds the premise
  against it, as the toys of `harness/trial32/` asked DOS/32A.

An implementation that models DOS, a file system in the memory that
behaves "as FreeDOS does", is what the rule forbids, behind our own
interface as much as in front of it. It holds what we believe of DOS:
the order of a directory, which error, what is left in AX. The code is
then made to pass on it, and the bench disagrees, or is not asked. The
one use that such a thing may have is under a fuzzer, where it only has
to agree with itself and nothing that it shows is compared with
anything.

A wording for the rule was proposed. It is **not adopted**: the rule is
the user's, and this is here as what was proposed, no more:

> `sys.h` is the project's, and an implementation of it made for
> tests is a part of the program replaced. It answers what a test tells
> it, or what the real system was recorded answering on the bench, and
> knows nothing of its own of what a system does. What runs on it shows
> what the program does with those answers; that a system gives them,
> and that the program does as the original, only the bench shows.

### Its limits

- The goldens stay the only witness of what the original does. Nothing
  here records the original, and nothing here says what DOS does.
- The bench stays the gate: a step lands when it has passed its
  scenarios on DOS, as now. What runs on this computer is what is run
  while working, and where the bench cannot go. The implementation for
  DOS is tested on the bench alone, whatever else there is.
- What a unit test expects comes from reading the assembly. It holds a
  behaviour in place and says where a failure is; it certifies no
  fidelity. An expected screen written by hand would be a golden
  edited by hand under another name: a test of a routine holds cells
  and numbers that the routine is said to make, not screens.
- A scripted failure shows what the program does with an answer. That
  a system gives that answer, and that the original does the same with
  it, it does not show: for the 298 instructions of the table there is
  still no golden.
- A recorded trace is valid only while the program asks the same
  things in the same order. This is the session's reservation, and it
  is right; what there is to add makes it sharper, not weaker. Replay
  serves work that leaves the questions alone: pointers for segments,
  numbers widened, a routine written anew above `sys.h`, what is
  drawn into the program's own buffer. Any change to what the program
  asks of the system, one call more or two in another order, ends the
  trace of every scenario that passes there, and those are recorded
  again on the bench, from a run that has passed against the
  original's golden. The same holds, for all of them at once, of a
  change to `sys.h` itself. Two things keep this from being a
  trap. A replay that meets another question than was recorded fails,
  it does not pass on a wrong answer, so a stale trace is noticed and
  says that the bench is wanted. And a trace is what a golden of the
  tree's own was before a deviation was held by a patch: it shows that
  nothing has changed since it was recorded, and what made it right was
  the bench.
- The sanitizers and the coverage are of the build of this computer,
  another compiler's of the same source, in a memory laid out
  otherwise. A fault that only the layout of DOS makes they do not
  see, and one that they see may be the original's.

### What it needs of `sys.h`

This section asked a design of the layer, on 13 October 2026, to leave
room for it. Step 3 settled the design the next day as DOS's, `sys.h`
as it is, and the critical error has been a call back that the program
hands over since S2. What still stands in the way of an implementation
for tests, from what was read then:

- A decision of the program's under the seam: `AskEs` of the system's
  file makes the error 53h of a call that the user gave up, asks DOS for
  its extended error, and reads `md.ErrDat`. Every implementation has
  to do the same again.
- What DOS happens to do, in what the functions take and answer:
  `value` as DOS left AX where nothing failed, `flagged`, the functions
  with Bare in their names, the page and the colour of `ScreenType`,
  `FcbParse` and `FcbDelete`. Each is one thing more that every
  implementation and every trace has to do as DOS does.
- What the system keeps between two calls and no call names: the
  current drive and directory, the record of a search, how often the
  pointer was hidden.
- Nothing that a test can call to start the program, and `ProgramEnd`
  does not return.

### Open, for the user

- Whether a build of the program for DOS that writes out what it asks
  and what it is answered may exist, to derive traces from, where
  "Scenarios" has that no build is made for the tests. It would judge
  nothing: the build that is shipped is the one that is held against
  the goldens.
- Whether the rule gets the wording above, or another, before any of
  this is built.
- Two things need no implementation for tests and could be done now.
  Neither is started:
  - Sequences of keys made at random, on the bench, against the
    original and a tree, with one that differs kept as a scenario. It
    is the one thing here that looks for a mistake of the translation
    where nobody thought to write a scenario. One to two days, an
    estimate.
  - A first figure of the C's own code: which of its blocks never
    ran, from the log of QEMU that the scenarios' test reads already,
    where it looks today only at where each function begins. Half a
    day, an estimate. It says which blocks ran, not which way a branch
    went.

## The program saves its setup and its session by itself: decided, not started

On the user's word of 14 October 2026 (`CLAUDE.md`, step 3 of the
road), given while a layer was being designed and kept when that design
was set aside: the program saves its preferences and its session, the
panels' directories and cursors, the sort modes, the command line and
its history, by itself, when they change, after a short wait so that a
run of changes is one write, and when it is ended, on Linux by a signal
or by its terminal going; on every platform, DOS included. "Save setup"
and the setting "Auto save setup" go. On DOS that is a deviation, to be
declared when it is built. The rule of the harness for it: the
comparison of a scenario's disks leaves the setup file out, but in the
scenarios that are about the setup itself.

To settle when it is built: one file or two, and which field is in
which; where each lives, on DOS beside the program under names of 8.3;
how long a change waits; a write that an end in the middle of it leaves
whole; what two copies of the program running at once do with one file;
and what the scenarios about the setup hold, now that the file is
written when the setup changes and not by a command. The setup file
keeps the original's format, on the user's word of 14 October 2026
(`CLAUDE.md`, step 3), which works wherever DOS is emulated: the
design that was set aside had made it a format of the program's own
everywhere, and that is dropped.

## What the surveys of the layer found that step 6 needs

A layer designed from the platforms' side was surveyed on 13 and 14
October 2026 and set aside for DOS as the layer (`CLAUDE.md`, step 3).
Its documents and the decisions made for it are in the history, `git
log --diff-filter=D -- src/portable_c/LAYER.md src/portable_c/layer`,
and none of those decisions is on the road but three that the user
named again for Linux on 14 October 2026 (`CLAUDE.md`, step 6):

- **Decided.** Enter on a file that the program cannot run hands it to
  `xdg-open`. The PC's sixteen colours are drawn as DOS has them,
  exactly, in 24 bits where the terminal allows it. The screen is 80
  columns by 25 rows and no other size, whatever the terminal's. And
  the size of a file stays DOS's `u32`: a file of 4 GB or more is shown
  and copied as DOS would (`CLAUDE.md`, the sign).

What the surveys found of Linux that the implementation of step 6
meets, beside what `CLAUDE.md` decides there; read in the documentation
then, nothing tried:

- **Reading the screen back.** A terminal cannot say what a cell shows;
  the Linux console alone can, by `/dev/vcsa`. What `ScreenGet` reads
  after a command, the screen that the command wrote, is the
  implementation's own copy or nothing. The alternate screen, `?1049h`,
  keeps the panels apart from what a command writes, one shown at a
  time, as Midnight Commander's Ctrl-O does.
- **Drawing.** A terminal decides a character's width by its own table,
  and terminals disagree; the frames and Cyrillic are of ambiguous
  width (UAX #11), two cells in a terminal set up for East Asian text.
  Placing the cursor at each run loses at most a cell where one
  disagrees. A terminal without colours of 24 bits has only the 16
  named ones, which are the user's theme; blinking is not everywhere.
  An update may tear without synchronized output, mode 2026 (xterm has
  it, st not). `TIOCGWINSZ`, and `SIGWINCH` when it changes, say only
  whether the 80 by 25 fit; the cursor is DECTCEM and DECSCUSR; a
  scroll is DECSTBM with SU and SD.
- **Keys.** Bytes on standard input in raw mode, read with a timeout;
  Esc and Alt with a letter both begin with ESC and are told apart by a
  timeout unless the protocol says. Ctrl with a letter is a control
  character, so Ctrl and Ctrl-Shift are one. A modifier alone, a key let
  go and a repeat come only by the kitty protocol, flags 2 and 8: kitty,
  Alacritty, foot, Ghostty, iTerm2, WezTerm, Windows Terminal and
  xterm.js have it, macOS Terminal and the Linux console not. Without
  it `KeysHeld` has nothing to answer: no tap on Alt, no key bar of
  Shift, Ctrl and Alt. The kitty protocol's flag 4 adds the key of a US
  layout, "Ctrl+С on a Cyrillic layout reports c", which is what the
  BIOS's scan code is for the speed search by Alt with a letter. A
  terminal has F1 to F12; the desktop keeps some, Alt-F4, and Alt-F7
  under some window managers.
- **The mouse.** `?1000h`, `?1002h` and the SGR form `?1006h`, in cells,
  with Shift, Alt and Ctrl, where the terminal keeps Shift for
  selecting text as a rule. A double click is the program's to measure.
- **The country.** `setlocale(LC_ALL, "")` by `LANG`, `LC_*` and
  `LC_ALL`; a locale that is not installed leaves "C". glibc's ru_RU
  has `%d.%m.%Y`, `%T`, and U+202F, three bytes of UTF-8, for the
  thousands; en_US `%m/%d/%Y` and `%r`. DOS's record, 38h, has one order
  of three and a byte for each separator. None of it is read for now: the
  code page is 437 and the country with it, always, on the user's word of
  14 October 2026 (`CLAUDE.md`, step 6).
- **Names.** Bytes, any but `/` and NUL, UTF-8 by custom and not by
  rule; 255 bytes, a path up to 4,096 and no hard limit. ext4 tells
  case apart, so two names of DOS's form may be one; two forms of
  Unicode are two names. A name that begins with a dot is hidden by
  custom; system and archive mean nothing, and permissions are the
  mode's bits.
- **Files.** `rename` replaces a target that is there, where DOS fails
  (`renameat2` with `RENAME_NOREPLACE` does not), and fails with
  `EXDEV` across file systems. A time is UTC to the nanosecond, DOS's
  local to two seconds from 1980 to 2107. `off_t` is 64 bits: a file of
  4 GB or more is shown and copied as DOS would, as decided above.
  `statvfs` gives the blocks
  free to the user and their size. A listing is `readdir` and a
  `fstatat` or `statx` for each entry, `d_type` maybe unknown, with no
  pattern. Mounts are in `/proc/self/mountinfo`, removable media under
  `/media`, `/run/media` or `/run/user/.../gvfs`.
- **Errors.** `errno`: `ENOENT`, `ENOTDIR`, `EACCES`, `EPERM`, `EROFS`,
  `EBUSY`, `ETXTBSY`, `EIO`, `ENOSPC`, `EDQUOT`, `ENOTEMPTY`, `EXDEV`,
  `EINTR`, each to be made a number of DOS's. There is no critical
  error: a drive that is not ready fails, `EIO` or `ENOMEDIUM`, and a
  network or FUSE mount may wait without end.
- **Programs and the program's life.** `$SHELL -c`, and `/bin/sh` where
  `SHELL` is not set; `system` ignores SIGINT and SIGQUIT while it
  waits; 127 where the shell or the command could not start. The
  terminal goes to a command with its modes put back, `tcsetattr` and
  `tcsetpgrp`, and a command may leave it odd. Ctrl-C is byte 03h with
  `ISIG` off; Ctrl-Break has nothing; Ctrl-Z stops by SIGTSTP where
  `ISIG` is on, and the program redraws on SIGCONT; SIGTERM and SIGHUP
  end it, the terminal to be put back first. The program's own file is
  `/proc/self/exe`; `xdg-open` answers 0, or 1 to 4 for an error, and
  does not wait for the program that it starts; a user's settings are
  in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `~/.config`, where the program's setup file,
  the original's `VC.INI`, is `vc/vc.ini` (`SetupFile` of
  `paths_posix.c`); the state and a command history in
  `$XDG_STATE_HOME`; temporary files in `TMPDIR` or `/tmp`.
- **Waiting and time.** `poll` on the terminal with a timeout, where DOS
  has INT 28h. `clock_gettime` with `CLOCK_REALTIME` and `localtime_r`
  for the time of day; `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`, which stops while the machine
  sleeps, or `CLOCK_BOOTTIME`, which does not, for the BIOS's ticks.

## Step 6: the program for Linux

The road of `CLAUDE.md`, step 6: `sys.h` for 64-bit Linux, built with
clang by the one `CMakeLists.txt`, emulating DOS at the level of its
services, beside `sys_dos.c` and `sys_stub.c`. Its first piece, L1, is
the part of the emulation that has no input or output of its own and is
tried on the host by itself.

### L1, drives, names, code page, dates, errors: done, and what L2 should know

What it made, a commit: four files of the implementation for Linux and
their header, `emulate_posix.h`, which says what each function answers,
in DOS's terms; and the test `portable_c-posix-unit`,
`harness/posixcheck.c`. Nothing of it is compiled into `VC.EXE`, which
is the same bytes, `2b6cc9b5...`.

- `codepage_posix.c`: the code page, 437: the character of Unicode of
  each byte, by Unicode's mapping file `CP437.TXT`, as Python's codec
  has it, from which the table was written; DOS's capitals of a byte of
  a name; a capital of Unicode made small; UTF-8, strict as RFC 3629 has
  it.
- `names_posix.c`: what a name of DOS's form is; the alias of a name of
  the host; a directory's table of names for the run; DOS's attributes
  of a file of the host.
- `paths_posix.c`: where the setup file is; a path of DOS's made a full
  one, as `DOS_MakeName` of DOSBox makes it; a full path of DOS's on C:
  to one of the host, and back.
- `time_posix.c`: DOS's packed date and time of a time of the host, and
  DOS's error of an `errno`.

The sources, each named in the test at its checks:

- **The capitals and what a name may have** are the bench's DOS's:
  FreeDOS 1.4's `COUNTRY.SYS`, from `x86BOOT.img` of the pinned
  `FD14-FloppyEdition.zip` (`mcopy -i x86BOOT.img
  ::/FREEDOS/BIN/COUNTRY.SYS`), read by its format: the table `FUCASE`,
  DOS's capitals for names (INT 21h 6504h), and `FCHAR`, what ends a
  name, of the country 1 with 437. Of 437 most accented
  small letters become a plain capital, é `E` and â `A`: a check written
  from memory had é `É`, and the table said otherwise. The bench of the
  United States names no country, and its kernel has its own table,
  which was not looked at: `KERNEL.SYS` is packed by UPX.
- **The alias** is fatgen103's short name, the basis name and the
  numeric tail: capitals, `_` for what the code page has not or a name
  may not have, spaces and leading dots left out, 8 characters in front
  of the first dot and 3 behind the last, and `~1` and up where anything
  was lost or the name is taken, `LONGNA~1`, `LONGF~10`. A change of case
  alone is no loss: `readme.txt` is `README.TXT`. Names are given in the
  order of their bytes when a directory is first read, and later ones
  behind them; a name keeps its alias for the run, and one that has gone
  keeps its alias from every other, so that a panel that was read before
  never names another file by it. Of two names that differ only in case
  the first keeps the plain name: `README.TXT` before `readme.txt`, and
  `readme.txt` before a `README.TXT` that comes later.
- **A byte that is not UTF-8** in a name of the host is `_` in the alias,
  which is then lossy and has a tail, `CAF_~1.TXT` of `caf\xE9.txt`; the
  table keeps the host's bytes, so the alias leads back to them exactly.
  Nothing else carries such a byte: no name of the program's has it.
- **The attributes**: DOSBox's localDrive gives every file of the host
  archive and a directory that of a directory, and nothing else of its
  own; read-only of the mode, by the bits of the owner, the group or the
  others as POSIX's `access` picks them, any of the three for the
  superuser; hidden for a name that begins with a dot, but `.` and
  `..`; never system, never a label. A directory is never read-only:
  DOS lets a file be made in one that is, and `/usr` would be so.
- **The full path** is `DOS_MakeName`'s: `/` for `\`, `.` and `..`
  worked out, `..` at the root staying there, each name in capitals and
  cut to 8 and 3, a second dot or a character that a name may not have
  error 3, a drive that is no letter 0Fh. `*` and `?` are taken, as a
  path to look for may have them. A drive other than C: is made full
  from its root, and is 0Fh, invalid, when its path of the host is
  asked for (RBIL, INT 21h 0Eh and 47h).
- **A date and a time**: DOS's packing (RBIL, INT 21h 5700h), in the
  local time; before 1980 the first that DOS has, 1 January 1980 at
  midnight, after 2107 the last, 31 December 2107 at 23:59:58, as Linux
  writes them on a disk of DOS's (`fs/fat/misc.c`,
  `fat_time_unix2fat`); an odd second is the even one before.
- **The errors**, by RBIL's calls and DOS's extended errors: `ENOENT` 2,

the mode, and three zeros, as the BIOS's data has them where
`harness/dos.py` reads them. `ProgramEnd` writes an `end ` record and
ends with its code; where the steps are done and the program waits for a
key all the same, it writes an `end ` record with 2, says on standard
error that the keys have run out, and ends with 2.

**The first run**, in a temporary directory under `/tmp` with `HOME`
there, under `posix-asan/vc`: the program comes up, draws its banner,
the panel, the command line and the key bar, takes Esc, Tab, Ctrl-F1,
Ctrl-F2, F1, F9 with Esc, Alt-F1 with Esc, Ctrl-L, Down, F3, F7, F8 with
Esc, and F10 with Enter, writes a screen for each step, saves `vc.ini`,
and ends with 0 and no sanitizer finding; 0.26 seconds, the sanitized
and the other alike. Its first screen against the golden of `start`,
the plainest: the colours of the frame, the titles and the key bar are
the golden's (1Bh, 1Eh, 30h, 07h), and the names and the cursor's shape;
what differs is what the masks of L3b or the scenario's own setup cover:
- the path, `C:\TMP\VCL3A~1.5GL\HERE` where the bench has `C:\WORK`, and
  the prompt's length with it, so the cursor's column;
- the files, of the host's directory, and the date and time of `..`;
- the setup: with no `vc.ini` the program takes its defaults, the left
  panel off, where the bench gives every scenario the setup file that
  the original saves (`CLAUDE.md`, "Scenarios"): L3b puts that file at
  `$HOME/.config/vc/vc.ini`;
- what DOS showed behind the panels: the bench has DOS's lines above the
  program's banner, scrolled; here the screen is empty when the program
  starts, so the banner is on its first two rows and the rest blank;
- the Info panel: no label, and the drive's room of the host's file
  system, 4,294,901,760 bytes, the most that DOS's shape holds (L2);
- F1 shows nothing, since `VC.HLP`, the help file of the shareware
  distribution, is not in `~/.config/vc`: L3b puts it there as the
  bench puts it beside the program, from the pinned download.

**Found by the sanitizers, and fixed in the common code** (each the
same behaviour on DOS; the scenarios judge the program for DOS):
1. `LnStr` of `line.c` read the byte behind a line's end, as the
   assembly's `LODSW` does: `Var_S` is `"^V"`, and the byte behind its
   zero is behind the object. Nothing went by it; the second byte is
   read now only where the first is not the end. (AddressSanitizer,
   global-buffer-overflow.)
2. `Dialog` of `dialog.c` read the place of the byte 0 that ends a
   dialog's fields, 2 bytes behind `Quit_B`, before it looked at its
   type; it looks first now, and leaves the loop for any type that is no
   field, as the `else break` did. (AddressSanitizer.) The second loop
   of `Dialog`, the keys of the field at the cursor, reads the place
   before the type too, and would read so behind a dialog whose first
   field is the end: none was seen.
3. `Rnd` of `input.c`, the random numbers, wraps at 16 bits as the
   original's: the two casts are written, with `wraps`. (The sanitizer
   of implicit conversions.)

**The alignment, left out of the sanitized build, for the session to
decide.** UBSan's `alignment` stopped the first run at a read of a word
at an odd place, `*(u16 *)text` of `Dialog`, which is one of the 128
casts and 33 structures laid over bytes that 5a listed: the common code
reads a word at any place of its bytes, as DOS does, which x86-64 does
as DOS does and C does not promise, and 5a left how they are read to
the layer. `posix-asan` has `-fno-sanitize=alignment` for that, with
the reason in `CMakeLists.txt`. A build with that check recovering, run
through the same keys, named three places: `dialog.c` 980 and 983 (the
input field's cursor, a word at `INPUT(control)`), and `read.c` 549. To
hold them, each such read becomes a `memcpy` or a function of `vc.h`
that reads a word of bytes, a piece of its own across the 23 files.

**What L3b should know:**

- The program is `build/portable_c/posix/vc`, and `posix-asan/vc` beside
  it; neither needs a terminal with `VC_TEST` set. A run wants `HOME` (or
  `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`) of its own, with the bench's setup file at
  `.config/vc/vc.ini` and the files that the bench puts beside the
  program there; and a current directory whose path DOS holds in 63
  characters, as `/tmp/...` does where a checkout's `build/` may not.
- A scenario's steps become lines of `keys`; a key with Shift, Ctrl or
  Alt wants `held=` around it, as the bench's BIOS has the key held
  while it is pressed: the program looks at `KeysHeld` for some. The driver's
  event of the timer is `wait=`; the mouse has none yet.
- The program ends by itself only through `ProgramEnd`; a scenario whose
  last step leaves it at its panels ends with 2 and an `end ` record.
- `AutoTim` is read by the channel in `md`, as the driver reads it in the
  machine's memory.
- `tools/figures.py` counts the build for DOS, whose figures moved by
  the three fixes, and was written. `harness/hostcheck.txt` and `harness/words.txt` have
  `sys_posix.c`, clean and with no word; `harness/stubcheck.py` reads it
  with the command of `posix-unit` (its top says why), and the build of
  `posix-unit` leaves it out, for its `main`.

What the next pieces meet:

- The bench's right panel, with every golden derived again: done, and

Decided by the user on 13 October 2026 (`CLAUDE.md`, "The portable C";

the name without a version in the box of F10, the line that asks for
Enter, and the top of the Info panel. `main_t.c` has the two texts as

title and the banner's first line, `NameVer_S`, the Info's title, and

The Info panel. Its two lines on the memory are gone, as something that

`panel.c` writes the first three and `PutInf` of `info.c` begins at the

How it is held. Four rules of `TREES["portable_c"]`, each a `Part`: the
part as the original shows it and as the portable C does, made to a

in their places, cell for cell, with what covers the part left as the

What is left out of the comparison. The count of free memory in the

### Put off: eight scenarios that could leave the Info off

Put off on purpose, on 13 October 2026. Eleven scenarios switch the Info
on as their first step and so have it on every screen, as before. For
three that is what they are about, `memory`, `dirinfo` and
`view-window`. The other eight could be written so that the Info is on
only where a step wants it, or not at all, which is what the change of
the bench was for. They were mended the short way all the same: with
`Ctrl+l` in front, every screen behind it is the old golden's cell for
cell, and that was the proof that the change of the bench lost nothing.
A scenario written anew has a golden to be read, and proves nothing of
the kind; it is worth doing once the proof is no longer needed, and not
before. What each would need, none of it tried but where it says so:

- `copy-big`: "F5", "Enter", "p", five times, repeats a copy by the
  last target, which F5 offers only next to the Info. With the name
  typed each time, `"huge" Enter`, it needs no Info. Tried: it leaves
  the same files.
- `move`: steps 4 and 5, F6 and Enter "onto itself", lean on F6
  offering the name of the file; next to files it offers their
  directory and the file is moved there. The name typed, or the Info on
  for those two steps.
- `rename-keys`: only its last three steps want the Info, as the
  current panel. `Ctrl+l` in front of them; the dialogs of the steps
  before then have `C:\` for a target, which is not what they are
  about.
- `copy-ask`: "offers its own name" and "offers the last target" are of
  a panel next to the Info, and three steps want the Info as the active
  panel. Next to files the same keys offer `C:\`, which is another
  thing to show and wants its own steps.
- `compare`: its first step, `Ctrl+c` that does nothing next to the
  Info. `Ctrl+l`, `Ctrl+c`, `Ctrl+l` in a row would have the Info on
  two screens where it is on nine.
- `reread`: its second step looks at what the Info says of a directory
  named dirinfo; the Info could go behind that step, where it goes at
  the twelfth.
- `menu`: one look, the Right menu of the Info, with the bar open from
  the second step to the twentieth. The look would move to a place
  where the Info can be switched on in front of it and off behind.
- `mouse-menu`: one click on an item that is dark, Compare directories

## Leaving a part of the screen out of the comparison: future work

Recorded on the user's word of 13 October 2026, as an idea for later. It
is not built, and nothing needs it today.

What it is. A golden stays what it is, every cell of every screen that
the original showed: it is the only witness of the original, and
recording the whole screen costs nothing. What changes is the
comparison, for one tree: a named part of the screen is left out of it,
"what the Info panel shows", "what DOS had shown behind the panels",
where that part cannot be what the original's is and is on many screens
that are about something else. It is the same thing that
`harness/deviations.py` does today for single figures, the count of free
memory and the clock, made larger. It is not a golden that records
less.

What raised it. Giving the portable C its own name touched the top rows
of the Info panel, which the distribution has on the right, on some
2,000 screens of scenarios that have nothing to do with it. That case
was settled otherwise: the bench now starts every scenario with a panel
of files on the right ("Scenarios" in `CLAUDE.md`), which takes the
part off those screens and leaves every cell that remains compared.
Where a part can be taken off the screen by how the bench is set up,
that is the better way.

Where it will be wanted. Where a part cannot be configured away: above
all the first build that is not for DOS, in which what DOS had shown
behind the panels is not there at all, and whatever of the Info panel a
system does not have, a label of a drive, the size of a disk as DOS
counts it, differs wherever the panel shows.

What it has to be, if it is built:

- Declared, for one tree, by the name of the part and the reason, in
  `src/portable_c/DEVIATIONS.md` like any other difference.
- By the part, not by a rectangle. A menu or a box drawn over the part
  is not left out with it: only the cells that show the part are. That
  takes knowing which cells those are on a screen where something
  covers some of them; one way is to leave out a cell only where the
  golden has, at that place, what the part has there when nothing covers
  it.
- Every part that is left out is still compared whole in at least one
  scenario that is about it, and the test says so if none is.

What it costs. The comparison of whole screens notices harm in places
that nobody was looking at: a count that was wrong in the editor showed
only in a status line drawn elsewhere on the screen (the note on
`T75_00` in `CLAUDE.md`). Inside a part that is left out, that is given
up. So a part is left out when nothing else will do, and as small as
will do.

For whoever designs it: the rules of `harness/deviations.py` that
belong to one tree should be able to say "these cells are not compared"
as well as "expect this in their place".

## The last of the assembly

Done: the C translation has no assembly file, and its build runs no
assembler for it. The assembler that the build fetches, JWasm, builds the
original from `src/asm/`, which the tests hold the translation against and
hold against the shipped binary, and the driver of the tests. This is a
short account of how the rest went, for whoever reads the history.

When every routine was C, `src/c/asm/` still held the data and the glue.
It went in this order:

1. The texts, boxes, dialogs, buttons and colours, a file of the
   assembly at a time, into files of constants, `src/c/*_t.c`, by the
   recipe in `CLAUDE.md`, "Moving the data of a file to C": several
   agents side by side, each with one file. The test `c-data` held every
   object against the original's bytes while it moved (below).
2. The words of a dialog that name a routine, which became numbers that
   `Dialog` goes by.
3. The commands and the main loop. A command was a label that the loop
   jumped to and that jumped back; each is a function that the loop
   calls from a `switch`, and the tables of the menus hold commands by
   their numbers. With the stubs went ten files. `Stay` of
   `src/c/resident.c` calls the rest of the program as one function,
   `TrnMain` of `src/c/main.c`.
4. The data and the stack of the part that stays in the memory, which
   are of `src/c/resident.c`; the word with the main data's segment,
   `SecDat`, a variable of `src/c/main_t.c`; and last what the one file
   left, `VC.ASM`, still said without an instruction or a byte of data:
   how the program is laid out. That is said by two options of the
   compiler and by the linker's command, and held by `tools/mkexe.c`:
   the README has it under "The C translation", and each place that rests on
   the compiler under "What rests on Open Watcom". The layout of the
   main data that the file had, its `STRUC`, nothing read any more:
   `struct MainDat` of `src/c/vc.h` is the only one.

What the last step found, beyond what the README says:

- The group of the constants, `DGROUP`, does not begin at the PSP any
  more, since nothing of C can hold it there: the first bytes of the
  file are of the other group. A word of a box that names a text is an
  offset in that group, whatever it begins at, and `AsmSeg` is its
  segment. Three places took the group to begin at the PSP: `Init11` of
  `src/c/start.c`, which worked out the length of a block from the
  segment of the constants; `Stay`, which read a far address in a
  constant at its offset in the segment `RunPar`; and `Alloc0`, which
  read a text of the rest through DS.
- The part that stays names something of the part that goes by its
  segment as the linker has it, to which it adds where that part is:
  `TRN_SEG` of `src/c/resident.c`. `tools/mkexe.c` keeps such a word out
  of the table of relocations.
- `md` is still an `extern` object, named to the linker as `Psp`. A
  layout at the number 0 does not work with this compiler, and neither
  does one based on the data segment: `CLAUDE.md`, "C for the translation",
  has why.
- Looked at and not taken: an object file without code or data that a
  tool writes, for the segments and the groups, which would do the same
  and is neither C nor the linker's command; the code of the part that
  stays in a segment of its own, which wants the vectors, `SetBrk`,
  `Exit01` and INT 2Eh told another segment than the PSP's; and the
  data linked in front of the code, which puts that code behind the
  stack, on the page that QEMU is slow on.

### What holds the data

The test `c-data`, `harness/datacheck.py`, holds every object of the
translation that has the name of an object of the original against the
original's bytes, without a machine: 96 constants of the C code, 2,976
bytes, and 373 objects of the assembly, 8,545 bytes, when it was made, and
469 objects of the C code, 11,973 bytes, now that all are C. It names
each. A word that holds an address is held by what it names: the
original's source is assembled once more as an object file, whose
relocations say which words those are, and the translation has to have at
such a word the address of what has that name in the translation. So nothing
describes an object to the tool; an object is written with the names of
the assembly and the linker does the rest.

It found five constants of the C code that were not as the original, all
texts with a zero byte behind them that the original has not. Four made
no difference, and are exact now: `SubDir`, `Ctrl_S`, `Byts_S`, `MenuLn`.
The fifth did: the end of the banner, `CrLf_S`, is copied as far as a
zero byte, and the original copies the text behind it along,
`Press ENTER to return`, into the buffer that DOS writes from as far as
the dollar sign. The C has the texts in one array now and copies as the
original does. No screen shows it.

What it does not hold, each listed in the tool with the reason:

- Constants that the original has not as data: `PowersOfTen`, `Panel_T`,
  `Scan_P`, `Fnc_T`. And of the part that stays in the memory the seven
  numbers that `tools/mkexe.c` writes, and `Stays`, what that part
  keeps, which is zeros in the file; and `TrnBeg`, the room of a
  block's header, zeros too.
- `Suff_S`, the edition in the banner: it lies in room that is reserved
  for what only the shipped binary has.
- Data that became code: the tables of keys are `switch` statements, and
  the scenarios answer for them.
- The tables by which the stubs of the commands went on, which are
  gone with them, `Main_T`, `CmdNx_T`, `MnuNx_T` and `F35_T`: they are
  `switch` statements of `src/c/main.c`, as the tables of keys are.

The tables of the menus' commands it holds in a way of their own. The
original has the address of a command for every item; the translation has
the number of the command, a `CMD_` of `src/c/vc.h` that is named after the
original's label, and the test reads those numbers there: an item that
has another command than the original's fails it.

What is read behind the end of an object is held too, as far as the
code says how much that is: a name copied as 13 bytes, a path as 68, a
title as 80. `harness/reads.py` lists every place where code names a
constant with the bytes read there, 400 places, and the test fails for
an object that is shorter, for a text read to a zero byte that has
none, and for a place it does not know (see "What is read behind the
end of an object" in `CLAUDE.md`). Eighteen texts are written longer
than the assembly has them for this; `User_S` was the last found.

Weighed against that, and not done: the constants laid out as one
block in the original's order, so that what follows each object is the
original's by construction. What it would take: the original's two
segments of data are 13,096 bytes; the translation has 11,568 of them under
their names, in thirteen files of constants and some ninety arrays that
the code files read through CS, and the rest is gone, tables of keys
that are `switch` statements and tables of addresses. One block is one
file in the original's order with filler for what is gone; the arrays
of the code files out of the code segments, so that each of some two
hundred places that read one by its name reads through a far pointer; and the
arrangement by file given up, which let five agents move the data side
by side. What it would cure beyond the sweep is nothing that is known.
The reads that the sweep cannot make good, the menu that is none and
the 88 bytes of a panel's defaults, go on into addresses of routines
and into what is no data, and a word that holds an address is another
number in the translation wherever it stands. What the block would have and
the sweep has not is that it needs no reading of the code: the tool
goes by the text of the C, and a read that it takes for another form
than it is would pass.

## Known and not dealt with

- The setup program is not translated. `VCSETUP.COM` exists only as the
  assembly of `src/asm/`, some 24 KB of it, which the test `asm-bytes`
  builds and holds against the shipped binary; no C tree has it, and no
  scenario runs it. It goes into the portable C, as a part of the one
  program: "The setup program in the portable C: the plan" at the top
  of this file. The C translation stays without it.

- The number of bytes that the editor has free is not compared with the
  original's (see `harness/deviations.py`). What works it out is C now,
  in `T00_20` of `src/c/edit.c`, and the number still wants a check of
  its own: that it falls by one for every character typed, at least.
  It has been wrong once without a test saying so, when a stub that it
  called handed back another CX. Held against the original by hand when
  the editor's keys were translated, over some thirty steps of
  `editor-keys`, `editor-hex-keys` and `editor-buffer`, in text and in
  hex: 27,104 less in each, 331,648 for an empty text, with the translation
  at 90,560 bytes.
- Saving in the editor to a disk that cannot be written, the floppy A:
  of the bench, with the box of DOS's critical error, is in no scenario:
  it went beyond the stack of 256 bytes that the translation had when the
  editor's saving was translated. With the stack of 4,096 bytes it can go
  back into one.
- `T80_00` takes what the program knows of the main extension file from
  the editor's text after saving it, and does so whether the file was
  written or not: a save of VC.EXT that fails changes what the program
  goes by until it is started again. Ported like that. Saving to the
  console writes nothing and is no error; and after a save under another
  name that fails, the new name is in the status line only once that is
  drawn again for another reason. Ported like that too.
- A disk that is full cannot be made on the bench, so what `T80_00` does
  then, deleting what it has written, rests on reading; and so does
  what it does when DOS refuses the attributes of a file just written.
- The harness can type Russian on the Russian bench, and nothing beyond
  ASCII on the other: Alt with the numeric keypad types nothing there.

- The screen blanker is C, `Blank` of `src/c/blank.c`, and what it draws
  is held against the original on no screen. Its stars come out where
  the program's random numbers say, and nothing sets the two words that
  those are made of, `Rand1` and `Rand2`, when the program starts: the
  sky follows from what the memory held where the main data is. On the
  bench that is 0 for the original, and something else for the translation,
  whose main data is elsewhere, another thing with every build. So a
  step may not end in the blanker. The scenario `blank` brings it up,
  with the mouse in the top right corner, and ends it in the same step,
  by a key, by the mouse moving away, by Shift and by a button: what the
  goldens hold is that the screen and the cursor come back and that the
  key is lost. If the program set the two words when it starts, a step
  could end in the sky and a golden could hold it; that would be other
  behaviour than the original's, and is not decided.
  The C was held against the original by hand instead, once, outside
  the tests: with the translation's two words set, in a build made for it,
  to what the original's are when the blanker comes up first, and with a
  step that lets the program go round without ending, both were taken
  through a sky of some hundreds of turns, and every screen of either
  was one that a model of the routine, written from the assembly, has
  after some turn. See what the batch lost time to, below.
- Of `LeaveTm`, six instructions of the original have run in no
  scenario and are listed as out of reach: they are for DESQview. The
  portable C has nothing for DESQview any more
  (`src/portable_c/DEVIATIONS.md`, 3).
- `ClsLine` fills a row with the colour that DOS writes in, and reads
